washing away a thousand years of heroes.
West of the old ramparts, men say,
was Zhou Yu’s Red Cliff of Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
fierce waves crash the shore,
flinging up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land—like a painting—
how many heroes once graced that hour!

I think of Gongjin in his prime,
newly wed to Xiao Qiao,
his heroic bearing, his spirit blazing.
With feather fan and silk cap,
amid his talk and laughter,
the enemy’s masts and hulls turned
to ash and vanished.
A wanderer in that vanished realm,
should you laugh at me for my feelings—
my temples already silvered?
This mortal world is but a dream.
Let me pour one cup
to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Washing away the distinguished figures of a thousand ages.
To the west of the old fortress, they say,
Lies Red Cliff of Zhou Yu in the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startling waves crash the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
This land and rivers are like a painting,
How many heroes it saw in its time!

I think of Gongjin in those years,
When Xiao Qiao was newly wed, with heroic bearing and brilliant spirit.
With a feather fan and silk scarf,
As he talked and laughed, the great ships
Were turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders to that ancient land,
How those who feel deeply would laugh at me,
For my temples have prematurely turned white.
The human world is like a dream,
So I pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。

Washing away the ages' gallant souls.
West of the ancient ramparts, men say,
Lies Zhou Lang's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Fierce waves crash the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The landscape is like a painting;
Of heroes, how many in that time!

I think of Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao was newly wed,
His heroic bearing, bright and dashing.
With a feather fan and silken cap,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
The enemy's masts and ships turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders to that ancient land,
The sentimental one should laugh at me,
For my temples have turned white too soon.
The world is but a dream;
I pour a libation to the river, to the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Washing away, through a thousand years,
Heroes of glory and grace.

West of the ancient ramparts, they say,
Lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Fierce waves crash the shore,
Piling ten thousand crests of snow.

The landscape is a painting—
In that one time, how many heroes rose!

I think of Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao was newly his bride, his heroic spirit shining.
With a feather fan and a silk scarf,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
Enemy masts and ships flew to ash, annihilated.

My spirit wanders to that former kingdom;
The sentimental one should laugh at me,
For my hair has turned white too soon.
The human world is but a dream—
I pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

its waves washing away
the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress,
people say, stands Red Cliff of Zhou Yu,
hero of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
fierce waves crash the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—
how many heroes once gathered here!

I think of Gongjin in his prime,
just married to Xiao Qiao,
so valiant and gallant.
With feather fan and silk scarf,
while he talked and laughed,
enemy ships turned to ashes and smoke.
My spirit wanders to that ancient realm—
if my feelings make me laugh,
it is for my early-greying hair.

Life seems but a dream.
I pour a cup of wine
in offering to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The great river flows east,
Its waves have washed away the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress,
They say it is the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu from the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash upon the shore,
Piling up into drifts of snow.
The rivers and mountains are like a painting—
How many heroes were there at that time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his youth,
Xiao Qiao had just been married to him,
His heroic bearing was radiant and bold.
With a feather fan and a silk scarf,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
The enemy's masts and hulls were reduced to flying ash and smoke.
My soul wanders to that ancient realm,
If my feelings were deep, they should laugh at me—
For white hair has grown too soon.
The human world is but a dream;
I pour a libation to the moon over the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The great river flows east,
Its waves have washed away the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress,
They say it is the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu from the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash upon the shore,
Piling up into drifts of snow.
The rivers and mountains are like a painting—
How many heroes were there at that time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his youth,
Xiao Qiao had just been married to him,
His heroic bearing was radiant and bold.
With a feather fan and a silk scarf,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
The enemy's masts and hulls were reduced to flying ash and smoke.
My soul wanders to that ancient realm,
If my feelings were deep, they should laugh at me—
For white hair has grown too soon.
The human world is but a dream;
I pour a libation to the moon over the river."}

The land is like a painting—
How many heroes once were here!

Just wed to Xiao Qiao, a hero in his prime.
With feather fan and silk cap,
In easy talk, the enemy ships were burned to ash.
I roam the old kingdom in a dream;
If I am moved to tears, then laugh at me—
My hair has turned white too soon.
Life is but a dream; I pour a cup

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The romantic figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress, they say,
Stands Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms days.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startling waves strike the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The landscape is like a painting—how many heroes once were here?

I think far back to Gongjin in those years,
When Xiao Qiao was newly wed, his heroic form inspiring awe.
In feather fan and silk cap, amidst his cheers,
Enemy masts and oars turned to ash and smoke.

My soul wanders to that ancient land,
They should laugh at my many feelings, that early I've grown white of hair.
The world is but a dream; I pour a cup of wine
To the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。

遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress, they say,
Lay Zhou Yu’s Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms’ rage.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves crash on the shore,
Rolling up a thousand piles of snow-white spray.
The mountains and rivers are like a painting, where once
So many heroes held their sway.

I think of Gongjin in his prime, when Xiao Qiao was his young bride,
His heroic bearing, his spirit soaring high.
With a feather fan and a silk scarf, in talk and laugh,
The enemy ships turned to ash and smoke before his eye.
My soul wanders to that ancient land, a sentiment I can’t hide;
They should laugh at my early grey hair, a feeling I can’t deny.
Life is but a dream, so I pour a cup of wine
To libate the river and the moon in the sky."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The romantic figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress, they say,
Stands Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms days.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startling waves strike the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The landscape is like a painting—who were the heroes of yore?

I think far back to Gongjin in those years,
When Xiao Qiao was newly wed, his heroic form inspiring awe.
In feather fan and silk cap, amidst his cheers,
Enemy masts and oars turned to ash and straw.

My soul wanders to that ancient land,
They should laugh at my many feelings, that early I've grown white of hair.
The world is but a dream, with a cup I toast
The river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The great river flows east,
Its waves have washed away
the romantic figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old ramparts,
people say, is Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
frightening waves beat the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
how many heroes there were in that time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his year,
when Xiao Qiao had just been married,
with a heroic bearing and brilliant spirit.
With a feather fan and a silk headband,
in his talk and laughter, the enemy's masts and oars
turned to ash and vanished in smoke.
My spirit wanders to that ancient kingdom—
if those with feeling were to laugh at me,
it would be for my hair turning white too early.
The human world is like a dream—
I pour a cup of wine to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Washing away the ages of heroes.
West of the old ramparts, they say,
Is Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged peaks pierce the sky, startling waves

The land is like a painting—
How many heroes once graced this scene.
I think of Gongjin in his youth,
When Xiaoqiao had just become his bride, his bearing heroic.
A feather fan, a silk kerchief, in his talk and smile
The enemy's masts and oars were turned to ash and smoke.
I wander in spirit to that ancient kingdom—
If my old feelings laugh at me, it is for my early grey hair.
Life is but a dream; I pour a libation
To the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Washing away the ages' heroes.
West of the old fort, they say,
Lies Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves
Beat the shore, rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.
The land is like a painting—how many heroes
Once flourished here.

I think of Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing, bright and bold.
Fan in hand, cap of silk,
In his talk and laughter, the enemy's
Masts and ships turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders to that ancient land—
If I seem over-sentimental, laugh at me:
My hair has turned white before its time.
Life is but a dream; I pour a cup
To the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Washing away the ages' gallant figures.
West of the old ramparts, men say,
Lies Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startling waves slap the shore,
Rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.
The land, like painting—
How many heroes in that one age!
I think of Gongjin in those years,
When Xiaoqiao had just become his bride, his bearing heroic and bright.
Feather fan and silk cap, in the midst of talk and laughter,
The masts and hulls were struck to ash and smoke.
My soul roams that vanished kingdom; if men of feeling laugh at me,
It is for the white hair that comes too soon.
All life is but a dream—
I pour a cup to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Washing away the ages' brilliant men.
West of the ancient ramparts, men say,
Lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves crash the shore,
Rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
How many heroes in their prime!

I think of Gongjin in those years,
When Xiaoqiao had just become his bride, heroic and dashing.
With feather fan and silk hat,
In easy talk, the enemy's masts and hulls turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders back to that kingdom;
If my feelings laugh at me, it is for
The early grey at my temples.
All the world is but a dream—
I pour a cup of wine to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Washing away, through the ages,
The heroes of a thousand years.

West of the old ramparts, they say,
Lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Fierce waves crash upon the shore,
Rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.

The land, like a painting—
How many heroes of that time!

I think of Gongjin in those years,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing, bright and bold.

With a feather fan and silk scarf,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
The enemy's masts and hulls were reduced to ashes and smoke;

My soul wanders to that ancient kingdom.
If I am too emotional, you should laugh at me—
My hair has turned white all too soon.

Life is like a dream—
I pour a cup of wine to the river and the moon."}

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。

遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。

its waves washing away
the heroes of a thousand ages.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
frightened waves beat the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—
how many heroes rose in that age.
I think of Gongjin in his prime,
just wed to Xiao Qiao,
heroic and brilliant.
Fans of feathers, silk hat,
in his talk and laughter—
masts and hulls turned to ash and smoke.
A dream of the old realm,
if I feel too deeply, laugh at me
for graying too soon.
Life is but a dream;
I pour a cup to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The romantic figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortress, they say,
Stands Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms days.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startling waves strike the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The landscape is like a painting—who were the heroes of yore?

I think far back to Gongjin in those years,
When Xiao Qiao was newly wed, his heroic form inspiring awe.
In feather fan and silk cap, amidst his cheers,
Enemy masts and oars turned to ash and straw.

My soul wanders to that ancient land,
They should laugh at my many feelings, that early I've grown white of hair.
The world is but a dream, with a cup I pour a libation
To the river and the moon."}

Frightened waves strike the shore, and spray
Up piles of snow-white foam.
The land is like a painting; how many heroes filled the hour.

I think of Gongjin in his prime,

With feather fan and silk cap, calm and sublime,
Amidst talk and laughter, the enemy fleet was burned and died.
Roaming the land of old, in a trance of time,
If love of life moves you, laugh at my early gray hair's chime.
Life is but a dream; I pour this cup to the river moon."}

With feather fan and simple silk cap, at his calm laughter, the enemy's warships turned to ashes and smoke.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Its waves have washed away
the gallant figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old ramparts, they say,
stands the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
startling waves batter the shore,
rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
how many heroes there were in that time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his youth,
just after Xiao Qiao had become his bride,
his heroic bearing brilliant and bold.
Feather fan and silk scarf,
in the midst of talk and laughter,
the enemy masts and hulls were turned to ash and smoke.
Roaming in spirit to that ancient realm,
those who are sentimental would laugh at me—
my temples have already turned grey.
Life on earth is but a dream;
let me pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

Feather fan and silk cap, in talk and laughter, the masts and hulls turned to ash and vanished in smoke.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。

With feather fan and silk scarf, he laughed calmly as warships turned to ash and smoke. 

In spirit I wander through the lost realm, perhaps my longing should make me laugh—my hair already frosted by time. 
Life is but a dream; I raise my cup, offering wine to the moon above the river."}

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

washing away all the noble figures of a thousand ages.

lay Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
 Jagged rocks pierce the sky, terrifying waves strike the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
how many heroes there were in that one time.

I think back to Gongjin in his prime,
just married to Xiao Qiao, majestic and brilliant,
with feather fan and silk cap,
and in the midst of talk and laughter,
the enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders to that ancient kingdom—
surely my sentimentality should make me laugh,
for my temples have already turned grey.
The world is but a dream;
I pour a cup of wine in offering to the river moon."}

Rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.

White hairs have already come too soon.
All life is but a dream—
I pour a cup to the river and the moon."}

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

Waves have washed away, through the ages, all brilliant figures.

The land and rivers like a painting—how many heroes in that moment.
I recall Gongjin’s prime: Xiao Qiao newly wed, his heroic bearing vividly bright.
With feather fan and silk scarf, at ease—warships turned to ashes in laughter.
My spirit wanders through the ancient land; tender-hearted, it would mock me—gray hairs sprout too soon.
The world a dream—raise one cup, pour it to the river moon."}

I roam in spirit through that ancient land,
And if my too-much-feeling heart should laugh, it would understand
That white already crowns my brow too soon.
All life is but a dream — I pour this cup to the river moon.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

sweeping away the ages' heroes of a thousand years.
West of the old ramparts, they say,
lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startled waves
slap the shore, rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—how many heroes
there were in that one age!

I think back to Gongjin in those years,
just wed to Xiao Qiao, his heroic bearing
vivid and spirited. With feather fan
and silk cap, amid his talk and laughter,
the enemy's masts and oars were blasted
to ash and vanished in smoke.

My spirit roams that ancient realm; if those
with feeling laugh at me, it is for the white hairs
that come too soon. The world is like a dream—
I pour a cup in offering to the river and the moon."}

With a feather fan and a silk cap, in the midst of talk and laughter, the enemy ships were reduced to ash and smoke.

With feather fan and silk scarf, at ease in talk, the enemy's warships turned to ashes in an instant.

With feather fan and silk scarf, he laughed and spoke, and the enemy ships turned to ash and smoke.

With feather fan and silk scarf, he laughed calmly—then the warships burned to ashes.

With feather fan and silk scarf, calm in his smile, the warships turn to ashes in an instant.

With feather fan and silk scarf, in calm command, the enemy’s warships vanish like smoke and dust.

With feather fan and silk scarf, at ease in conversation, the enemy fleets turned to ashes in an instant.

With a feather fan and silk scarf, he laughed and spoke, and the warships were reduced to ashes in an instant.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

All the brilliant figures of history.
West of the old fortress, it’s said—
Three Kingdoms’ Zhou Yu, at Red Cliff.

Rocks pierce the sky, surging tides crash against the shore,
Rolling up thousands of snow-white heaps.
The land and rivers, a painting of grandeur—
How many heroes arose in that moment!

I recall Gongjin in his prime:
Xiao Qiao newly wed, his heroic bearing radiant.
With feather fan and silk scarf,
Calmly speaking, warships turned to ashes, vanished.

My spirit wanders through the ancient realm—
Would the tender-hearted gods laugh at me,
For gray hairs sprouting too soon?

Life is but a dream.
I raise my cup, pour wine to the moon above the river."}

With feather fan and silk scarf, he laughed and talked, and the warships turned to ashes in an instant.
Dreaming of the lost land, I think: how sadly tender-hearted ones would laugh at me, already gray-haired.
Life is but a dream; I raise my cup and pour wine to the moon over the river."}

With a feather fan and silk scarf, he laughed and talked, and within moments the enemy ships were reduced to ashes.

Life is but a dream; I raise a cup and pour wine to the moon over the river."}

With feather fan and silk scarf, in calm talk, warships turned to ashes, vanished like smoke.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The land and rivers form a painting so bright—how many heroes emerged in that fleeting moment!

I dream of Gongjin in his youth—when Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, his spirit soaring, his charm shining bright.
With feather fan and silk cap, a mere word from him—and the warships turned to ash in the breeze.
My soul wanders through the ancient land—how the tender-hearted must laugh at me, for I’ve grown white-haired too soon.
Life is but a dream—let me pour this cup as offering to the moon above the river."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

The Great River flows eastward,
Its waves have washed away
A thousand ages of romantic heroes.

West of the ancient ramparts,
They say, stands the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves slap the shore,
Rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.

The land and rivers are like a painting—
How many heroes, in that one time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his youth,
When Xiao Qiao had just married him,
His heroic bearing, brilliant and spirited.

With feather fan and silk headband,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
The enemy's masts and oars were reduced to ashes and smoke.

My spirit wanders through that ancient kingdom—
If my excess emotions make me laugh at myself,
Early have I grown white at the temples.

The human world is like a dream;
I pour one cup of wine to the river and the moon."}

乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。

羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

West of the old fortress, they say it was here, at Red Cliff, where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.
Rocks pierce the sky, towering and wild;
Tidal surges crash against the shore,
Whirling up thousands of heaps like snow.
Like a painting, the land and rivers, so magnificent—how many heroes arose in that era!
I recall the young Gongjin of yesteryears:
When Xiao Qiao was newly married, his vigor radiated bright and bold.
With feather fan in hand, silk scarf around his neck,
In calm laughter, the enemy's warships turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders through that ancient land—how gently sorrowful I must seem to be, already gray-haired before my time.
Life is but a dream; I raise my cup and pour wine to the moon over the river."}

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,

rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the tune of Nian Nu Jiao: Reflections at Red Cliff

The great river flows east,
Its waves have washed away
The gallant figures of a thousand ages.
West of the ancient ramparts, they say,
Lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Startling waves crash upon the shore,
Piling up a thousand drifts of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
How many heroes there were in that time!

I think far back to Zhou Yu in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing, his dashing spirit.
With a feather fan and a silk kerchief,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
The enemy's ships were reduced to ashes and smoke.
My soul wanders to that ancient kingdom—
If those impassioned spirits still live,
They should laugh at me,
For my temples have already turned white.
All life is but a dream;
I pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A Thousand Ages of Rivers and Mountains

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains — where now
the hero, that is, Sun Zhongmou?
Terraces of dance and song, their elegance all
beaten away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes
and alleys, they say once dwelt "the Guest".
Think of those years — golden spears and iron steeds,
spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuan Jia's rash venture, seeking to seal the Wolf Altar,
won only a panicked glance to the north.
Forty-three years — in my gaze I still remember
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back? Beneath the Fox Spirit Shrine,
a flock of crows and the drums of the village festival.
Who will ask whether old Lian Po,
though aged, can still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the tune of Niannujiao: Reflections at Red Cliff

The Great River flows east, its waves
Washing away the ages' heroes.
West of the ancient ramparts, they say,
Lies Zhou Yu's Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startling waves
Beat the shore, rolling up a thousand snows.
The land is like a painting—
How many heroes once graced this scene!

I think of Gongjin in those years,
When Xiaoqiao had just wed him, his heroic bearing bright.\nWith feather fan and silk cap,
In easy talk, the enemy fleet
Vanished in smoke and ash.
Wandering in spirit to that old realm,
You should laugh at me for growing early white hair.
The world is but a dream—
I pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

To all the ages, mountains and rivers remain,
But heroes have vanished — Sun Zhongmou is nowhere to be found.
Dance-halls, singing-platforms, their elegance and charm
Are always swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun o'er grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
Men say the place where Jinu once stayed.
Imagine those years of golden halberds and iron steeds,
Breath swallowing a hundred miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia acted rashly, aiming to seal Wolf Mountain,
Only to win a hurried, glancing-back retreat.
Forty-three years have passed, and in the distance I still remember
The beacon-fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back — beneath the temple of Foli,
A flock of crows and the drums of the village shrine?
Who is there to ask: old Lian Po,
Can you still eat your fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**Eternal Joy: Meditations at Beigu Terrace, Jingkou**

To all the ages, mountains and rivers remain,
But heroes have vanished — Sun Zhongmou is nowhere to be found.
Dance-halls, singing-platforms, their elegance and charm
Are always swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun o'er grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
Men say the place where Jinu once stayed.
Imagine those years of golden halberds and iron steeds,
Breath swallowing a hundred miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia acted rashly, aiming to seal Wolf Mountain,
Only to win a hurried, glancing-back retreat.
Forty-three years have passed, and in the distance I still remember
The beacon-fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back — beneath the temple of Foli,
A flock of crows and the drums of the village shrine?
Who is there to ask: old Lian Po,
Can you still eat your fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The mighty river rolls eastward, its waves scouring away all the heroic spirits of antiquity.
West of the ancient fortifications, it is said—here stood Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms, where Zhou Lang once led his men.
Riven boulders cleave the sky, crashing billows beat the shore, heaving up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and rivers like a scroll painted in splendor—how many heroes rose in that fleeting age.
Longing back to Gongjin’s days, when Xiao Qiao had just been married, his noble bearing aflame with spirit.
Feather fan in hand, silk hat on head, amidst his laughter, the enemy ships crumble to dust.
My spirit wanders through the ancient realm—were others to see me, they’d surely laugh at my longing, with gray hair sprouting too soon.
Life on earth is but a dream; I pour this wine upon the river, honoring the moon."}

by Su Shi

The great river flows east,
its waves washing away
the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old ramparts—
such is the local tale—
stands the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
fierce waves crash the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—
how many heroes once gathered here.

I think of Gongjin in his prime,
just wed to Xiao Qiao,
majestic and resplendent,
fans of feather, caps of silk—
in his talk and laughter,
the enemy fleet turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders back to that ancient realm;
surely the sentimental one should laugh at me,
for my hair has turned white so soon.
Life is but a dream—
I pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

The Great River flows east, its waves
Washing away the brilliant figures of a thousand ages.

Lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu, hero of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Fierce waves crash upon the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—how many heroes of that time!

I think of the young Zhou Yu then,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, his heroic bearing brilliant.\nWith a feather fan and silk scarf,
In the midst of laughter and talk, the enemy ships were reduced to ashes and smoke.

Human life is but a dream—
I pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

With feather fan and silk cap, in calm discourse—before his gaze, the war galleys turned to ash and vanished into smoke.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the Tune of Nian Nu Jiao: Reflections at Red Cliff

By Su Shi

The Great River flows eastward,
Its waves have washed away
A thousand years of brilliant figures.

West of the ancient ramparts,
People say,
Lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Frightening waves strike the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.

The rivers and hills are like a painting,
How many heroes of that time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just married him,
His heroic bearing, bright and spirited.

With a feather fan and silk cap,
In the midst of talk and laughter,
The enemy's masts and oars vanished in smoke and ashes.

My spirit wanders back to that ancient land,
If my heart is too emotional, laugh at me—
Already my hair has turned white early.

Life on earth is like a dream;
Let me pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A Thousand Ages of Rivers and Hills

A thousand ages of rivers and hills—
no sign of the hero, not where Sun Zhongmou stood.
Dance platforms and song stages:
all their glory washed away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
lanes and alleys common as any—
they say this is where Zhu Nu once lived.
Think of those years:
bronze halberds and iron horses,
a force that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
In the Yuanjia haste,
they sought to crown wolf-beacon hill,
and won only a panicked glance back north.
Forty-three years on,
looking out, I still recall
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Under the Foli Shrine,
ravens croak and festival drums drone.
Who will ask—
is old Lian Po still able to eat his rice?"}

Where empires rise and fall through endless time,
No hero's trace is found where Sun once stood.
The terraces for song and dance, where grace sublime
Once reigned, are swept away by wind and flood.

Sloping sun on grass and trees, in lanes so plain,
They say the Founder's home once stood right here.
Recall those days when spears and chargers in the plain
Breathed tiger's might that swallowed all things far and near.

Yuan Jia's rash plans to carve the Wolf Mount's crest
Only won a frantic glance back to the north.
Forty-three years on, in my eyes still expressed,
I see the beacon fires on Yangzhou's path of worth.

How could I turn my head to see again
The Fox's shrine below, with black crows and drums?
Who would ask if old Lian Po, beyond the ken
Of age, can still eat rice and lead his drums?"}

Rocks jut wild into the sky, waves

The great river flows east, its waves
Washing away, through the ages,
All the heroes of a thousand years.

As people say,
Stands Red Cliff of young General Zhou of the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Fierce waves crash upon the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.

The land is picturesque;
How many heroes rose in that brief time!

I think of young Zhou Yu then,
When he had just wed Xiao Qiao,
With his heroic bearing and spirited air.

In the midst of easy talk and laughter,
The enemy's masts and oars (or: the fleet) were reduced to ashes and smoke.

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。

West of the old fortress, they say this is where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms fought at Chibi.
Rough rocks pierce the sky, thundering waves crash against the shore, rolling up thousands of heaps like snow.
A landscape so beautiful—what heroes arose in that moment!
I recall Gongjin in his prime, newly wed to Xiao Qiao, his vigor radiant and strong.
With feather fan and silk cap, calm and smiling, the warships turned to ashes in an instant.
Lost in reverie among the ruins of that ancient land, I imagine my own deep feelings must seem foolish—my hair already streaked with gray.
Life is but a dream; I raise a cup, offering wine to the moon above the river."}

No hero to be found, where Sun Zhongmou dwelt.
Dance-halls and singing-towers,
The elegance is gone, beaten by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
They say, is where the guest-slave once stayed.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron horses,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia rushed headlong, to seal Wolf Ridge,
Only to gain a hasty glance back northward.
Forty-three years—gazing still, I remember,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back: beneath Foli's shrine,
A flock of crows, the drums of the village festival.
Who will ask: Is Lian Po old now,
Can he still eat his fill of rice?"}

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains—
No trace of heroes, nor of Sun Zhongmou's reign.
Dance halls and singing terraces,
All elegance swept away by wind and rain.

Beneath the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
On common lanes and streets, they say,
The homestead of Liu Yu once stood.
Imagine then: with spear and armored horse,
His spirit swallowed miles, fierce as a tiger.

Yet Yuanjia rushed into war,
Seeking to seal the wolf on Mount Jushi—
And won only a panicked glance to the north.
Forty-three years have passed,
When I gaze north, I still recall
The beacon fires over Yangzhou's roads.
How can I bear to look back?—
Beneath the shrine of Foli the Barbarian,
Crow-crows and drumbeats fill the air.
Who will ask, as they asked of Lian Po:
'The old man—can he still eat his rice?'

(*Sun Zhongmou: Sun Quan, King of Wu during the Three Kingdoms.
Liu Yu, styled Jì Nú: founder of the Liu Song dynasty.
Yuanjiao: era name of Emperor Wen of Liu Song.
Mount Jushi: where the Han general Huo Qubing celebrated victory over the Xiongnu.
Foli: the Northern Wei emperor Tuoba Tai, whose shrine stood south of the Yangtze.
Lian Po: the aged Zhao general, doubted in his old age.*)"}

By Xin Qiji

The river and hills through the ages remain, but heroes are gone—
No trace of Sun Zhongmou to be found.
The dance-halls and singing-towers, their elegance swept away
By wind and rain, beaten down to dust.
Beneath the slanting sun, among grass and trees, in common lanes,
They say the cabin once was Ju Nu's home.
Think of those years—swords of bronze and steeds in iron mail,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.

In Yuanjia, hasty campaigns to carve a wolf's design on Mount Jushi,
Won only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years have passed; in my gaze I still recall
The beacon fires blazing on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back? Below the Foli Shrine,
Only crows of the altar and drums of the spring festival.
Who will ask me—like Lian Po, grown old,
Can he still eat his fill of rice and serve?"}

I recall those days: golden spears and iron horses, a spirit devouring thousands of miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign, sealing the wolf at Juxu, ended in frantic retreat northward.

How unbearable to look back—beneath the temple of Fuli, crows squawking, drums for the community feast.

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand ages of rivers and mountains—
nowhere to find a hero like Sun Zhongmou.
Dance-halls and singing-platforms,
their elegance all swept away
by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
an ordinary lane and street—
people say Liu Ju once lived here.
Think of those years:
 golden spears and iron-hoofed horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuan Jia's rushed campaign—
seeking to enfeoff at Wolf-terror Peak—
won only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years,
gazing from here I still remember
the beacon-fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
only crows and the drums of the spring festival.
Who will ask:
Lian Po is old—
can he still eat his fill of rice?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the tune “Nian Nu Jiao: Remembering the Past at Red Cliff”

The Great River flows eastward, its waves washing away
the heroes of a thousand ages past.
West of the ancient ramparts, men say
stands the Red Cliff where young Zhou Yu held sway.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves beat the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land is like a painting—how many heroes, in that hour!

I dream back to Gongjin in his prime, just wed to Xiao Qiao, his bearing proud and bright.
Feather fan and silk cap, in easy talk and laugh—the enemy’s masts and hulls turn to ash and smoke.
Wandering in this land of old, if my fond heart laughs at me, it is for the white hairs that come too soon.
All the world is but a dream; I pour a cup to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the tune of Nian Nu Jiao: Reflections at Red Cliff

The great river flows east,
Its waves have washed away
A thousand years of heroes.
West of the ancient ramparts, they say,
Stands Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Frightened waves crash the shore,
Rolling up a thousand drifts of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
How many heroes of that time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his prime,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
His heroic bearing bright with youth.
Feather fan and silk scarf,
In his talk and laughter,
The masts and oars turned to ash and smoke.
My soul roams his old kingdom—
If I am too sentimental, I should laugh at myself
For growing white hair so soon.
The human world is but a dream;
I pour a cup of wine to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**Eternal Joy · Recalling Heroes at the Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou**

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and hills—
Of heroes, no trace remains, where Sun Zhongmou stood.
The dancing terraces and singing stages,
All their elegance has been washed away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say the place where Ju Nu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.

Yuan Jia acted rashly,
Seeking to seal the wolf on Mount Junxu,
Only to win a hasty northward glance in panic.
Forty-three years have passed,
In the distance, I still remember
The beacons blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back—
Beneath the shrine of Emperor Feili,
A flock of crows and drums of the spring festival.
Who is there to ask:
I am like the aged Lian Po,
Can I still eat my fill?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**Eternal Joy · Recalling Heroes at the Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou**

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and hills—
Of heroes, no trace remains, where Sun Zhongmou stood.
The dancing terraces and singing stages,
All their elegance has been washed away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say the place where Ju Nu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.

Yuan Jia acted rashly,
Seeking to seal the wolf on Mount Junxu,
Only to win a hasty northward glance in panic.
Forty-three years have passed,
In the distance, I still remember
The beacons blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back—
Beneath the shrine of Emperor Feili,
A flock of crows and drums of the spring festival.
Who is there to ask:
I am like the aged Lian Po,
Can I still eat my fill?"}

No hero to be found, not where Sun Quan stood.
The dance terraces and singing platforms,
The elegance all driven off by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass and trees,
In an ordinary lane, they say Liu Yu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron horses,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign,
To title Wolf Peak,
Won only a panicked look to the north.
Forty-three years,
In the distance I still remember
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath Foli Shrine,
A flock of crows and drums of the spring festival.
By whom will it be asked:
Is Lian Po old, and can he still eat his fill?"}

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains—
nowhere to find a hero like Sun Zhongmou.
Dancing terraces and singing platforms,
their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.
Beneath the slanting sun, among grass and trees,
in some ordinary lane, they say once lived Jilu—
those years of golden spears and iron-clad steeds,
whose breath could swallow ten thousand li like a tiger.

In the Yuanjia era, [they] acted rashly,
seeking to seal Wolf Mount like Huo Qubing,
only to win a panicked retreat, gazing northward.
Forty-three years have passed—
across the view, I still remember
the beacon fires over Yangzhou Road.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the Temple of the Buddha Deer,
only cawing crows and festival drums.

Who will ask whether old Lian Po,
though aged, can still eat his fill?"}

Where once was Sun Zhongmou’s reign.
Terraces for dance, halls for song,
Their elegance washed away by wind and rain ere long.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In lanes and alleys commoner’s homes,
They say, once, Jiannu’s abode did rise.

Golden spears and war-horses,

In my gaze I still remember,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Crows of the god and drums of the rite.
Who will ask—
Can Lian Po, old and greyed,
Still eat his rice enough?"}

Where now to find the hero, great Sun Zhongmou?
Dance-halls and singing platforms, all their glory
Scattered and washed away by wind and driving rain.
Beneath the slanting sun on grass and trees,
In some common lane, they say the warlord once dwelt—
That Liu Yu of old. Think of those days:
With spear and armored steed, his spirit swallowed ten thousand miles,
Fierce as a tiger.
Yet Yuanjia's hasty campaign—
To raise a wolf-tower on Mount Ju—
Won only panicked glances cast behind in flight.
Forty-three years have passed,
And gazing north, I still recall
The beacon fires blazing along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of the Northern barbarian king,
Only crows around the altar drums and offerings.
Who will ask now—
Can old Lian Po,
Though past his prime,
Still fight?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Heroes nowhere to be found—
Where once lived Sun Zhongmou. 

Palaces of dance and song, 
All noble grace now swept away 
By rain and wind’s relentless blow. 

Sunset lingers on grass and trees, 
In common alleys, people say: 
Here dwelled the Emperor Ji, 
Who marched through war in golden armor— 
His spirit like a tiger, swallowing ten thousand li. 

But Yuanjia’s hasty and ill-prepared campaign, 
To replicate Han Wu’s victory at Langju, 
Only won a hasty glance northward in retreat. 

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my sight: 
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road. 

How can I bear to look again—
At the temple of Fuli, 
Where crows feast and drums beat for the gods? 

Who now dares ask—
Old General Lianpo, 
Can he still eat his meal?"}

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains—
no hero to be found, no trace of Sun Zhongmou.
Dance pavilions, singing platforms,
their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, ordinary lanes—
men say the place where Jinu once dwelt.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-hoofed horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia's haste, to seal the wolf at Junxu,
won only a panicked glance back north.
Forty-three years, gazing still I remember,
beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back?—
Bili Shrine below, a crowd of temple crows and festival drums.
Who will ask: Lian Po is old—
can he still eat his fill?"}

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains—no hero remains,
Where once Sun Zhongmou ruled, none to find.
Dance halls and singing terraces, all their splendor swept away
By wind and rain, beaten down and lost to time.
Beneath the slanting sun, on grassy trees,
An ordinary lane—one says a commoner dwelt.
Think of those days: golden spears and iron steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.
Yuanjia's haste, to seal the Wolf Mount, only earned
A panicked glance cast northward in retreat.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my gaze I remember
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back? Below the Foli Shrine,
Crows of the gods, the drums of spring rites, one unbroken sound.
Who will ask now: Is Lian Po old, can he still eat his rice?"}

Dance-halls and song-screens,

In lanes and streets of common fame—
They say here General Jinu once dwelt.

A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**Eternal Joy·Nostalgia at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou**

A thousand autumns, rivers and hills—
No hero left where Sun Zhongmou stood.
Dance-halls and song-screens,
All their elegance swept off by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In lanes and streets of common fame—
They say here General Jinu once dwelt.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed headlong,
To seal the Wolf on Mount Juxu,
But won only a hasty glance north in flight.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still I recall, in all I see,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How could I turn my head?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Crows croak, and temple drums beat.

Who will ask: Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat his fill of rice?"}

nowhere Sun Zhongmou remains.
Dance-halls and singing terraces,
their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass and trees,
common lanes and streets —
some say Jilu once dwelt here.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
their spirit swallowing ten thousand li like tigers.
Yuanjia recklessness — a hasty seal at Langjuxu,

beacon fires over Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back? Beneath Foli Temple,
a flock of crows and drums of the spring festival.
By whom will it be asked — is Lian Po old,
still able to eat his fill?"}

Thinking back then, with golden spears and iron horses, he swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign, sealing the wolf at Juxu, only won him a panicked retreat northward.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in memory, the fires along the Yangzhou road.
How unbearable it is to look back—where the temple of Foli stands, crows feast, and drums beat for the village gods.

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of rivers and hills,
No place remains where the hero Sun Zhongmou dwelt.
Dancing porches and singing terraces,
Their charm all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In an ordinary lane and alley,
People say Junu once lived.
Recall that year: golden spears, iron cavalry,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand *li* like a tiger.
Yuanjia was rash and hasty,
To crown Langjuxu with merit,
Only gained a panicked glance to the north.
Forty-three years have passed,
In my gaze I still remember the beacon fires on the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the temple of Foli,
A flock of crows and the drums of the village altar.
Who will ask:
Is Lian Po old,
Can he still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "To the tune of Nian Nu Jiao: Reflecting on the Past at Red Cliff

The great river flows east, its waves washing away
the heroic figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old fortifications,
people say this is the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves slap the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting—
how many heroes of that one age!

I think far back to that year when Gongjin was young,
when Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, his bearing heroic and brilliant.
With feather fan and silk cap,
in the midst of talk and laughter, the enemy masts and hulls vanished in smoke and ashes.
My spirit wanders to that ancient kingdom;
if my feelings were to laugh at me, they would say my temples have already turned grey.
Life in the world is but a dream—
I pour one cup of wine to libate the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of rivers and mountains,
Where heroes once stood—now nowhere to find
At the spot of Sun Quan.

The halls of dancing, the platforms of singing—
All now reduced to dust beneath the rain and wind.

Sunset through grass and trees,
In ordinary alleys, they say
Li Tu once lived.

I recall those days:
Golden lances flew, iron steeds charged—
A force that swallowed the world, swift as a tiger.

Yuanjia’s rash campaign,
To emulate the sealing at Langjuxu—
Only to flee in panic, looking back northward.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still burning in memory:
The beacon fires across the land of Yangzhou.

How can I bear to look back—
At the temple of Fuli—
Crows peck at offerings, the village drums beat in vain.

Who dares inquire:
Old General Lian Po—
Still fit to eat his rice?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of rivers and mountains,
Heroes nowhere to be found—
Where Sun Zhongmou once reigned.

Palaces of dance and song,
All glory and grandeur lost to time,
To rain and wind’s unyielding might.

Sunset lingers on grass and trees,
In common alleys, people say:
Here lived Liu Yu, known as Jiniu.

Who marched through war in golden armor—
His spirit like a tiger, vast and fierce—
Consuming ten thousand miles with might.

A hasty attempt at conquering Mount Langju,
Only brought panic at the northern frontier.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my sight:
The flames of war along the Yangzhou road.

How can I bear to look again—
At the temple of Fuli,
Where crows feast and drums beat for the gods?

Who now dares ask—
Old General Lianpo,
Can he still eat his meal?"}

Across a thousand ages, rivers and mountains —
no hero can be found
where Sun Zhongmou once stood.
Terraces for dancing, halls for singing —
all their elegance has been
beaten away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
common lanes and streets —
people say that Jinu once lived here.
Think of those years:

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
a flock of temple crows and drums for the village festival.
On whom can I ask:
Lian Po is old —
can he still eat his fill?"}

Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses, roaring like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of rivers and mountains, 
Heroes nowhere to be found— 
Where once lived Sun Zhongmou. 

Palaces of dance and song, 
All noble grace now swept away 
By rain and wind’s relentless blow. 

Sunset lingers on grass and trees, 
In common alleys, people say: 
Here dwelled the Emperor Ji, 
Who marched through war in golden armor— 
His spirit a tiger, devouring ten thousand miles. 

But Yuanjia’s rash campaign, 
Foolish ambition to conquer Mount Langju, 
Only brought panic at the northern frontier. 

Forty-three years have passed— 
Still vivid in my sight: 
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road. 

How can I bear to look again— 
At the temple of Fuli, 
Where crows feast and drums beat for the gods? 

Who now dares ask— 
Old General Lianpo, 
Can he still eat his meal?"}

Heroes nowhere to be found— 
Where once lived Sun Zhongmou. 

Palaces of dance and song, 
All noble grace now swept away 
By rain and wind’s relentless blow.

In common alleys, people say: 
Here dwelled the Emperor Ji, 
Who marched through war in golden armor— 
His spirit a tiger, devouring ten thousand miles. 

But Yuanjia’s rash campaign, 
Foolish ambition to conquer Mount Langju, 
Only brought panic at the northern frontier. 

Forty-three years have passed— 
Still vivid in my sight: 
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road. 

How can I bear to look again— 
At the temple of Fuli, 
Where crows feast and drums beat for the gods? 

Who now dares ask— 
Old General Lianpo, 
Can he still eat his meal?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Heroes nowhere to be found—
Where once lived Sun Zhongmou.

Palaces of dance and song,
All noble grace now swept away
By rain and wind’s relentless blow.

Sunset lingers on grass and trees,
In common alleys, people say:
Here dwelled the Emperor Ji,
Who marched through war in golden armor—
His spirit a tiger, devouring ten thousand miles.

But Yuanjia’s rash campaign,
Foolish ambition to conquer Mount Langju,
Only brought panic at the northern frontier.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my sight:
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road.

How can I bear to look again—
At the temple of Fuli,
Where crows feast and drums beat for the gods?

Who now dares ask—
Old General Lianpo,
Can he still eat his meal?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.

The pavilions where dance and song once flowed,
All are swept away by rain and wind’s cruel blow.

Sunset lingers on grass and trees,
In humble lanes where Li Tu once lived.
How I recall: the golden spears, iron horses,
Fierce as a tiger, devouring ten thousand miles.

Yet Yuanjia’s hasty campaign,
Seeking glory at Langjuxu, brought only panic in retreat.

Forty-three years pass like smoke in sight—
Still vivid, the flames along Yangzhou’s route.

How painful to look back—
At Buddha’s Shrine, crows cry, drums beat, spirits aglow.

Who dares ask: Old Lianpo, is he still strong?
Can he still eat his meal?"}

By wind and rain that beat them down.
Beneath the slanting sun, grass and trees,
In an ordinary lane,

Golden spears and iron-clad steeds,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

To wolf-shaped honors at Langjuxu,

Gazing afar, I still remember
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.

Beneath the Foli Shrine,
A flock of crows and the drums of village rites.
Who will ask—
Is Lian Po old now?

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Song pavilions and singing terraces, all that grandeur now battered by rain and wind.
Sunset lingers on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys, people say Liu Yu once lived here.
Thinking back, how valiantly he marched with golden spears and iron horses, his spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's campaign was hasty and ill-planned; seeking glory at Lang Juxu, he only earned frantic glances northward in retreat.
Forty-three years have passed—still vivid in my mind: the fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable it is to look back: beneath the Buddha Li Temple, crows cry, drums beat in frenzy.
Who dares ask—old General Lianpo? Still able to eat, isn't he?"}

Think of those days: golden spears, iron-hooved horses,

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

Singing pavilions, dancing terraces—glamour long since battered by rain and wind.
Sunset over grass and trees, through ordinary alleys, people say Li Bu once lived here.
Thinking back then: golden spears and iron horses, power swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, sealing the Wolf's Ridge, only earned frantic retreat northward.
Forty-three years have passed; even in sight, I still recall the flames along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable to look back—below the Temple of Fuli, crows clamoring, drums of sacrificial rites echoing.
Who dares ask: Lian Po, old as he is, can he still eat?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once roamed—
No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.

The pavilions where dance and song once echoed,
All are swept away by rain and wind.

Sunset stains the grass and trees;
In alleyways ordinary to the eye,
They say Liu Yu once dwelled here.

Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses,
Like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia’s rash campaign—
Foolish pursuit of glory at Langju,
Only to flee in panic northward.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my sight:
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road.

How bitter to look back now—
At the temple of Fuli, crows screaming, drums booming.

Who dares ask, “Is General Lianpo still strong?
Can he still eat?”"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once roamed—
No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.

The pavilions where dance and song once echoed,
All are swept away by rain and wind.

Sunset stains the grass and trees;
In alleyways ordinary to the eye,
They say Liu Yu once dwelled here.

Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses,
Like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia’s rash campaign—
Foolish pursuit of glory at Langju,
Only to flee in panic northward.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my sight:
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road.

How bitter to look back now—
At the temple of Fuli, crows screaming, drums booming.

Who dares ask, “Is General Lianpo still strong?
Can he still eat?”"}

Where once lived Sun Zhongmou.

Palaces of dance and song, all noble grace now swept away
By rain and wind’s relentless blow.

Sunset lingers on grass and trees,
in common alleys, people say:
Here dwelled Liu Yu, who marched in golden armor—
In his prime, with iron cavalry, he devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia’s campaign was hasty and ill-conceived;
to conquer Mount Langju, he rushed forward,
only to flee in panic northward.

Forty-three years have passed—still vivid in my sight:
the fires of war along the Yangzhou road.

How can I bear to look again—
at the temple of Fuli, where crows shriek and drums beat for the feast?

Who now dares ask—
Old General Lianpo,
Can he still eat his meal?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of rivers and mountains, 
Where heroes once roamed—no trace remains of Sun Zhongmou. 
The pavilions where dances thrived, the stages where songs echoed, 
All have vanished, swept by wind and rain. 

Sunset stains grass and trees, 
In alleys ordinary, they say Liu Yu once lived here. 
Recalling those days: 
Armored horses, iron spears, 
Mighty as a tiger swallowing ten thousand miles. 

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, 
Failed to secure the wolf's lair, 
Left only frantic glances back at the north. 

Forty-three years have passed— 
Still vivid in memory: 
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road. 

How unbearable to look back now, 
At the temple of Fu Li, 
Where crows feast and drums beat in frenzy. 

Who dares ask— 
Old General Lianpo, 
Can he still eat his meal?"}

The pavilions where songs once echoed,
All are now swept by wind and rain.

Recall those days:
Steel horses and iron blades,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign,

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vividly seen: the fires along the Yangzhou road.

Where once lay Sun Zhongmou's domain.
The pavilions where songs once soared, the halls where elegance reigned,
All swept away by rain and wind, long gone.

Sunset on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
They say Li Tu once lived here.
Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses,
Mighty as a tiger swallowing ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, seeking glory at Langjuxu,
Only left frantic looks toward the north in panic.
Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my gaze: flames along the road to Yangzhou.

How unbearable to look back—
At Buddha's Temple, crows flying, drums beating in frenzy.
Who will ask: Old General Lianpo, still able to eat?"}

Recalling those days: golden spears, iron horses,

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "A thousand years of rivers and mountains, 
Where heroes once stood—now nowhere to find 
Sun Zhongmou’s traces. 

The pavilions where dances thrived, 
The stages where songs once soared— 
All swept away by rain and wind. 

Sunset through grass and trees, 
In ordinary alleys, they say 
Li Tu once lived. 

I recall those days: 
Golden spears, iron horses, 
Fierce as a tiger swallowing ten thousand miles. 

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, 
Haste to seal the Wolf’s Gap, 
Yet fled in panic northward. 

Forty-three years have passed— 
Still vivid in memory: 
The flames along the Yangzhou road. 

How can I bear to look back— 
At the temple of Fuli, 
Where crows feast and drums beat for gods? 

Who dares ask: 
Old General Lian Po— 
Is he still strong enough to eat?"}

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains—
no hero to be found, not where Sun Zhongmou once reigned.

Terraces of dance and song,
their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
by common lanes and streets,
they say the place where Jinu once lived.

Think of those years—
golden spears, iron-hooved steeds,
a spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia's haste,
sealing the wolf at Mount Ju,
won only a frantic glance back northward.

Forty-three years,
gazing from here I still remember,
beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Bili Shrine,
a flock of crows, the drums of the spring festival.

By whom will it be asked—
Lian Po is old now,
still can he eat his fill?"}

No trace of heroes like Sun Zhongmou.

The dance pavilions, singing stages—
All their glory now swept by wind and rain.

Sunset among grass and trees,
Ordinary alleys where Liu Yu once lived.

Recall those days: iron horses, golden spears,
Giant strides devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia rashly—
To seal the wolf at Juxu,
Only to flee in panic northward.

Forty-three years later—
Still vivid in sight: 
Fires blazing along the Yangzhou road.

Who can bear to look back?
At the Temple of Buddha Li,
Crows cawing, drums thumping—divine clamor.

Who dares ask: 
Old General Lianpo—
Can he still eat?"}

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Where heroes once stood—now nowhere to find 
Where Sun Zhongmou once dwelt.

The pavilions where dances thrived,
The stages where songs once soared—
All swept away by rain and wind.

Sunset through grass and trees,
In ordinary alleys, they say
Li Tu once lived.

I recall those days:
Golden spears, iron horses,
Fierce as a tiger swallowing ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia's hasty campaign,
To emulate Huo Qubing's glory at Langjuxu,
Only to retreat northward in panic.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in memory:
The flames along the Yangzhou road.

How can I bear to look back—
At Fuli's temple,
Where crows feast and drums beat for gods?

Who dares ask:
Old General Lian Po—
Is he still fit for service?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once roamed—  
No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.  

The pavilions where dance and song once echoed,  
All are swept away by rain and wind.  

Sunset stains the grass and trees;  
In alleyways ordinary to the eye,  
They say Liu Yu once dwelled here.  

Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses,  
Like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.  

Yuanjia’s rash campaign—  
Foolish pursuit of glory at Langju,  
Only to flee in panic northward.  

Forty-three years have passed—  
Still vivid in my sight:  
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road.  

How bitter to look back now—  
At the temple of Fuli, crows screaming, drums booming.  

Who dares ask, “Is General Lianpo still strong?  
Can he still eat?”"}

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of rivers and mountains—where now
the hero Sun Zhongmou stands?
Wind and rain have scoured away
the elegance of terraces and singing halls.
Beneath slanting sun, grass and trees, in common lanes—
they say the house of Ji Nu once stood.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron steeds,
a tiger's breath consuming ten thousand miles.
Yuan Jia's heedless charge, seeking to seal the Wolf Steppes,
won only a frantic backward glance.
Forty-three years gone—still in my eyes,
the beacon fires of Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back? Below the Foli Shrine,
a flock of crows and drums for the harvest god.
Who will ask: is old Lian Po still able
to eat his fill and fight?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once stood—
Yet none can find the place of Sun Zhongmou.
The pavilions and stages, the elegance once grand,
Are now all battered by rain and wind.

Sunset lingers on grass and trees,
In lanes and alleys known to all—
It's said that Ji Lu once lived here.
Recalling those days: golden spears, iron horses,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

But Emperor Yuanjia’s hasty campaign,
Seizing the Wolf's Ridge in vain,
Left him fleeing northward in panic.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my mind: the fires of Yangzhou on the road.

How unbearable to look back—
At the temple of Fuli, crows cawing,
Drums beating for the village gods.

Who dares ask: Old Lianpo, though aged,
Can he still eat?"}

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "An Eternal Joy — Reflecting on the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Across the ages, this Land of Rivers and Mountains,
No hero can be found—where Sun Zhongmou once stood.
Dances on terraces, songs in pavilions,
All their elegance, swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
People say that Jinu once lived.
Think of that time—golden spears, ironclad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li, like a tiger.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal the wolf at Langju,
Won only a hasty flight, glancing north in alarm.
Forty-three years have passed, and in my gaze I still remember,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back? Beneath the Fuli Shrine,
A flock of temple crows and the drum of the village festival.
Who can ask—Lian Po is old,
Can he still eat his fill?"}

Across the ages, this Land of Rivers and Mountains,
No hero can be found—where Sun Zhongmou once stood.
Dances on terraces, songs in pavilions,
All their elegance, swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
People say that Jinu once lived.
Think of that time—golden spears, ironclad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li, like a tiger.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal the wolf at Langju,
Won only a hasty flight, glancing north in alarm.
Forty-three years have passed, and in my gaze I still remember,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back? Beneath the Fuli Shrine,
A flock of temple crows and the drum of the village festival.
Who can ask—Lian Po is old,
Can he still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once roamed—
No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.

The pavilions where dance and song once flowed,
All are swept away by rain and wind’s cruel blow.

Sunset lingers on grass and trees,
In humble alleys, they say Liu Yu once lived in these.
Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses,
Like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles of lands.

Yuanjia’s campaign, hasty and ill-planned,
Seizing the Wolf's Ridge, yet fled in panic, turning back.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in sight: firestorms along the Yangzhou road.

How can one bear to look back now—
At the temple of Fuli, crows cawing, drums thumping with zeal?

Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo,
Can he still eat his rice?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers—heroes nowhere to be found, not even Sun Zhongmou's place. 
The dancing pavilions and singing terraces, all that elegant grace, 
Have long since been battered by wind and rain. 
In the twilight, grass and trees line the humble lanes; 
They say Li Tu once lived here. 
Recalling those days: golden spears and iron horses, 
A spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger. 
Yuanjia’s campaign was reckless; he sought glory at Lianjuxu, 
Yet ended in panic, fleeing northward. 
Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my sight: the fires blazing along the Yangzhou road. 
How hard to bear the sight: 
At Buddha’s Shrine, crows caw, drums beat for the gods. 
Who dares ask— 
Old General Lianpo, is he still able to eat?"}

No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.
The pavilions where songs once echoed,
All are now swept by wind and rain.

Sunset over grass and trees,
In ordinary alleys, they say Li Tu lived.
Recall those days:
Steel horses and iron blades,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign,
To conquer Mount Langju, yet fled in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed—
Still vividly seen in memory:
The fires along the Yangzhou road.

How painful to look back—
At Fuli Temple, crows clamoring, drums beating for the gods.
Who will ask:
Old General Lianpo—is he still able to eat?"}

No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.
The pavilions where songs once echoed,
All are now swept by wind and rain.

Sunset over grass and trees,
In ordinary alleys, they say Li Tu lived.
Recall those days:
Steel horses and iron blades,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign,
To conquer Mount Langju, yet fled in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed—
Still vividly seen in memory:
The fires along the Yangzhou road.

How painful to look back—
At Fuli Temple, crows clamoring, drums beating for the gods.
Who will ask:
Old General Lianpo—is he still able to eat?"}

The dance pavilions, the singing stages—
All that grace and brilliance, worn down by rain and wind.

In common alleys, they say Li Tu lived here.
Recalling those times: golden weapons, iron horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Forty-three years past—still clear in vision:

At Foli’s Shrine, crows cry, drums beat for the god—

Not even where Sun Zhongmu stood, the master of his kind.
Terraces of dance and song, their elegance all gone,
Swept by wind and rain from the world they shone.

The setting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
They say the warlord Liu Yu once lived in these retreats.
Recall those days of golden spears and armored steeds,
A tiger's might that swallowed ten thousand miles of deeds.

Of beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou in the night.

The crows of heaven and drums of sacrifice, a raucous shame.
Who will ask of me now, like Lian Po in his old age?
Can I still eat enough rice, to prove I can wage war still, stage by stage?"}

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and hills—

The dancing terraces and singing stages,

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys,
People say the place where Ju Nu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.

Yuan Jia acted rashly,
Seeking to seal the wolf on Mount Junxu,
Only to win a hasty northward glance in panic.
Forty-three years have passed,
In the distance, I still remember
The beacons blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back—
Beneath the shrine of Emperor Feili,
A flock of crows and drums of the spring festival.
Who is there to ask:
I am like the aged Lian Po,
Can I still eat my fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of rivers and mountains—no hero can be found where Sun Zhongmou stood.
The dance-halls, the singing terraces,
their elegance, all of it, wind and rain have beaten down.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
in some ordinary lane and market street,
the people say that Liu Ji once lived there.
Think of those years—
golden spears, iron-clad horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li, fierce as a tiger.
Yuanjia rushed things,
to seal the wolf on Mount Juxu,
and won only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years on,
still I remember in the distance,
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back—
beneath the Foli shrine,
a flock of temple crows, the drums of the spring sacrifice.
Who will ask, when Lian Po has grown old,
can he still eat his rice?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of rivers and mountains, where heroes once stood—
Yet none can find the place of Sun Zhongmou.
The pavilions and stages, all that once was grand,
Are now battered by rain and wind, swept away by time.

The setting sun among grasses and trees,
In humble alleys, they say Li Tu once lived.
Recalling those days: golden armor, iron horses,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, seeking glory at Langjuxu,
Only left frantic retreats to the north.
Forty-three years have passed—still vivid in sight,
The flames along the road to Yangzhou.

How unbearable to look back now—
At Buddha's Temple, crows flying, drums beating in frenzy.
Who dares ask: Though old General Lianpo is frail,
Can he still eat?"}
