Across the ages, this land of rivers and mountains—
no hero can be found like Sun Zhongmou.
The terraces of song and dance,
all their elegance, swept away
by wind and rain.
Beneath the slanting sun, amid grass and trees,
in the common lanes and alleys,
they say the hut of Ji'nu once stood.
Think of those days—
golden spears and iron steeds,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign,
seeking to seal the peak of Langju,
won only a panicked retreat, glancing back north.
Forty-three years,
from here I still remember
the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
only crows and drums of the spring festival.
Who will ask—
is Lian Po old, indeed?
Can he still eat his fill?"}

Swept by wind and rain from the world they shone.

舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: At Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou, Recalling Antiquity

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—
No hero left to find, the place where Sun Zhongmu once was.
The terraces for dance, the stages for song,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
Men say the place once home to Jinu.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed to war, to seal a wolf on Mount Juxu,
And won only a panicked glance behind.
Forty-three years, and in my gaze I still remember,
Beacon fires blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How could one turn to look again—
At Foli's shrine, where a scene of sacred crows
And festival drums fills the air.

Who is there to ask:
Is old Lian Po,
Still able to eat his fill?"}

Through ages the rivers and hills remain—
Where now is Sun Zhongmou, hero supreme?
Dance terraces and singing stages, all their glory
Swept away by wind and rain and passing stream.

Beneath the slanting sun, grass and trees,
In lanes and alleys common and plain,
They say once the Founder made his home.
Think of those years—
swords of bronze, steeds of iron,
A spirit that would swallow ten thousand li like a tiger bold.

Yet Yuanjia's hasty campaign,
To seal the wolf on Mount Xuxu,
Won only a panicked glance back north.

Forty-three years have passed,
And gazing from this height I still recall
The beacon fires blazing along the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back—
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
The crows of the gods, the drums of the festival,
A single clamor of the crowd.

Who will ask: 'Is Lian Po old indeed?
Can he still eat his fill and fight?'"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of rivers and mountains, where heroes vanish—
No trace of Sun Zhongmou remains.
The pavilions of dance and song, the glamour once so bright,
Now all are battered by wind and rain.

Sunset on grass and trees, in lanes of common folk,
They say Li Tu once lived here.
Recall those days: iron horses, golden spears,
Fierce as a tiger, swallowing the world.

Wang's campaign was rash—
He sought to seal the mountain of Lanyu,
Yet fled in panic, gazing northward.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my sight:
The smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road.

How bitter to look back now—
At the temple of Fuli, crows crying, drums resounding,
A ghostly clamor of gods and village rites.

Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo,
Is he still strong enough to eat?"}

yet no hero can be found where Sun Zhongmou once held sway.
Dancing terraces and singing platforms:
all their glory, swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys—

A thousand autumns, this land and stream —
No hero's found, save only Sun Zhongmou's dream.
Terraces where dancers swayed, where songs did ring,
Their grace is gone — swept off by wind and rain's sting.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes so plain,
They say the great Jinu once lived here, they claim.
Recall those years: golden spears, iron-hoofed steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like fierce steeds.

Crows of the gods, and drums of the communal shrine?
Who would ask me — old Lian Po, his hair grown gray,
Can he still eat his fill and fight another day?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy at the North Fort Pavilion in Jingkou, Recalling the Past

A thousand autumns, this land and stream —
No hero's found, save only Sun Zhongmou's dream.
Terraces where dancers swayed, where songs did ring,
Their grace is gone — swept off by wind and rain's sting.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes so plain,
They say the great Jinu once lived here, they claim.
Recall those years: golden spears, iron-hoofed steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like fierce steeds.

Yuanjia rushed forth, to Feng Langjuxu they'd climb,
But won — just a hasty glance north, in dread and chime.
Forty-three years, in the distance I still see,
The beacon fires along Yangzhou's road, burning free.

How can one bear to look back — beneath Foli's shrine,
Crows of the gods, and drums of the communal shrine?
Who would ask me — old Lian Po, his hair grown gray,
Can he still eat his fill and fight another day?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: At Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou, Recalling Antiquity

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—
No hero left to find, the place where Sun Zhongmu once was.
The terraces for dance, the stages for song,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
Men say the place once home to Jinu.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed to war, to seal a wolf on Mount Juxu,
And won only a panicked glance behind.
Forty-three years, and in my gaze I still remember,
Beacon fires blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How could one turn to look again—
At Foli's shrine, where a scene of sacred crows
And festival drums fills the air.

On whom can one rely to ask:
Is old Lian Po,
Still able to eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once stood—
Yet none can find the place where Sun Zhongmou reigned.
The pavilions and singing halls,
All that elegant grace, now swept by wind and rain.

Sunset glows on grass and trees,
In common alleys, they say Liu Yu once lived.
Recalling those days—
Armored horses, iron warlords,
Their spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia’s campaign was rash and ill-planned,
Seizing Mount Lianxu, yet fleeing in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my gaze:
Fires burning along the Yangzhou road.

How painful to look back—
At the temple of Foli,
Where crows cry and drums thud with ritual dread.

Who dares ask—
Is old General Lianpo still strong enough to eat?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once stood—
Yet none can find the place where Sun Zhongmou reigned.
The pavilions and singing halls,
All that elegant grace, now swept by wind and rain.

Sunset glows on grass and trees,
In common alleys, they say Liu Yu once lived.
Recalling those days—
Armored horses, iron warlords,
Their spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia’s campaign was rash and ill-planned,
Seizing Mount Lianxu, yet fleeing in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my gaze:
Fires burning along the Yangzhou road.

How painful to look back—
At the temple of Foli,
Where crows cry and drums thud with ritual dread.

Who dares ask—
Is old General Lianpo still strong enough to eat?"}

Yet none can find the place where Sun Zhongmou reigned.
The pavilions and singing halls,
All that elegant grace, now swept by wind and rain.

Sunset glows on grass and trees,
In common alleys, they say Liu Yu once lived.
Recalling those days—
Armored horses, iron warlords,
Their spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia’s campaign was rash and ill-planned,
Seizing Mount Lianxu, yet fleeing in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed—
Still vivid in my gaze:
Fires burning along the Yangzhou road.

How painful to look back—
At the temple of Foli,
Where crows cry and drums thud with ritual dread.

Who dares ask—
Is old General Lianpo still strong enough to eat?"}

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and mountains—
No hero to be found, not even Sun Zhongmou's trace.
The terraces for dance, the platforms for song,
All their elegance, swept away by wind and rain.
Beneath the slanting sun, grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
They say that once the commoner Ji-nu dwelt.
Think of those years—swords of gold, steeds of iron,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li, fierce as a tiger.

Yuan Jia's hasty campaign, to enfeoff at Wolf Standard Hill,
Only won a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years have passed—
In my gaze, I still remember the beacon fires over Yangzhou's roads.
How can one bear to look back? At Foli's Shrine,
A flock of crows, the drums of the spring sacrifice.
By whom shall it be asked—
Has Lian Po grown old? Can he still eat his fill?

2. "寄奴"—Literally "the one entrusted as a slave," a childhood name of Liu Yu (later Emperor Wu of Song). The translation uses "the commoner Ji-nu" to retain the original's colloquial humility.
3. "仓皇北顾"—Could mean "a panicked glance back to the north" (the fleeing general looking north) or "a panicked northern region gazing back." The translation follows the former reading.
4. "佛狸祠下"—"Under Foli's Shrine" could imply "at the foot of" or "beneath [the shadow of]." The translation uses "At Foli's Shrine" to keep the location clear.
5. "尚能饭否"—Literally "can [he] still eat?" This alludes to the old general Lian Po's claim that he could still fight. The translation keeps the food metaphor ("eat his fill") while implying the broader question of continued capability."}

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of rivers and mountains, where heroes vanish—  
No trace of Sun Zhongmou remains.  
The pavilions of dance and song, the glamour once so grand,  
All have long since been swept by wind and rain.  

Sunset stains the grass and trees,  
In lanes I’ve known all too well—  
They say Li Tu once lived here.  
Recalling those days,  
Armored horses, iron weapons—  
A spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger.  

Yet Yuanjia’s campaign was hasty,  
His dream of sealing Mount Langju ended in panic,  
Fleeing northward in disarray.  

Forty-three years have passed—  
Still vivid in my sight:  
The fires of war along the Yangzhou road.  

How can I bear to look back?  
At Buddha’s Temple, beneath its ruins,  
Crows caw, drums beat for the village feast.  

Who will ask me now—  
Old General Lianpo—  
Can I still eat?"}

— Xin Qiji

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—where
Is the hero's like? Where is Zhongmou, Sun Quan?
Terraces for song and dance, all elegance and grace,
Swept away by wind and rain without a trace.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
Men say the place once sheltered Ju Nu's claim.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like fierce steeds.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjuxu,
Won them nothing but a panicked backward view.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my sight,
The beacon fires of Yangzhou Road burn bright.
How can I bear to look back? At Foli's shrine,
Crows of the gods, drums of the village rite align.
Who will ask if Lian Po, though old, has yet
The strength to eat his fill and not forget?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "An Eternal Joy: Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Immortal hills and rivers, here and now,
But no hero to be found, not even Sun Zhongmu's brow.
Terraces of dance and song, their elegance all gone,
Swept by wind and rain from the world they shone.

The setting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
They say the warlord Liu Yu once dwelt here.
Recall those days of golden spears and armored steeds,
A tiger's might that devoured ten thousand li.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjun in fame,
Won only a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years gone by, I still recall the sight,
Of beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

How could I bear to look again? At Foli Shrine below,
A scene of crows and drums.
Who will ask of me now, as Lian Po in his old age?
Can he still eat enough to serve?"}

Immortal hills and rivers remain,
Yet no hero like Sun Zhongmu can be found again.
Terraces of dance and song, their splendor washed away
By the wind and rain that erode all things in their day.

The setting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
They say that Jinu, of old, once made his home upon this seat.
Recall those days of golden spears and armored steeds,
A tiger's might that swallowed ten thousand miles of lands.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjun in fame,
Won only a panicked glance back north — a bitter shame.
Forty-three years gone by, from this vantage I recall
Beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou, burning all.

How could I bear to look again? Below Foli's shrine,
Crows of the gods, drums of rites — a sacrificial line.
Who will ask of me now, as Lian Po in his old years,
Whether he can still eat enough to quiet his fears?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "An Eternal Joy: Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Immortal hills and rivers, here and now,
But no hero to be found, not even Sun Zhongmu's brow.
Terraces of dance and song, their elegance all gone,
Swept by wind and rain from the world they shone.

The setting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
They say the warlord Liu Yu once lived here.
Recall those days of golden spears and armored steeds,
A tiger-like might that devoured ten thousand li.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjun in fame,
Won only a panicked glance northward in defeat.
Forty-three years gone by, I still recall the sight,
Of beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

How could I bear to look again? At Foli Shrine below,
A scene of crows and drums, the old rites' show.
Who will ask of me now, as Lian Po in his old age?
Can he still eat enough, to serve and fight?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

A thousand years of rivers and hills—
Where is the hero, Sun Zhongmou?
Only wind and rain
Still strike the terraces of song and dance,
Sweeping all glory away.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In common lanes and streets,
Men say Ju Nu once lived.
Think of that time—
Golden spears, iron-hoofed horses—
A breath that swallowed ten thousand *li*, fierce as a tiger.

Yuan Jia rushed to war,
Hoping to set up a shrine at Langjuxu,
But won only a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years,
And in my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires on the Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the Shrine of Foli,
Crows and the drums of the village festival.
Who will ask:
"Is Lian Po old?
Can he still eat his fill?""}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

A thousand years of rivers and hills—
Where is the hero, Sun Zhongmou?
Only wind and rain
Still strike the terraces of song and dance,
Sweeping all glory away.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In common lanes and streets,
Men say Ju Nu once lived.
Think of that time—
Golden spears, iron-hoofed horses—
A breath that swallowed ten thousand *li*, fierce as a tiger.

Yuan Jia rushed to war,
Hoping to set up a shrine at Langjuxu,
But won only a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years,
And in my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires on the Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the Shrine of Foli,
Crows and the drums of the village festival.
Who will ask:
"Is Lian Po old?
Can he still eat his fill?""}

By Xin Qiji

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and hills—
No trace remains of the hero Sun Zhongmou.
The dance-halls and singing-platforms,
All their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane—
They say the warlord Jingnu once dwelt here.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuan Jia rushed his campaign, seeking to seal the Wolf Altar,
Only to win a hasty flight, glancing back north in panic.
Forty-three years have passed—
In the distance I still remember the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
At the shrine of Fili, the temple crows and drummers for the spring festival crowd.
Who will ask:
"Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat his fill of rice?"

---
Notes on ambiguous readings in the original:
1. "英雄无觅，孙仲谋处" — could mean (a) "no hero like Sun Quan can be found in this place" or (b) "no place to find a hero like Sun Quan." The translation follows (a) but preserves the ambiguity.
2. "人道寄奴曾住" — "寄奴" is Liu Yu's nickname; "人道" ("they say") adds an oral-history flavor that resists precise rendering.
3. "赢得仓皇北顾" — "赢得" ("to win") is sardonic; the translation keeps the irony of "winning" a panicked retreat.
4. "佛狸祠下" — "佛狸" (Fili) is the posthumous name for Northern Wei Emperor Taiwu (Tuoba Tao); the shrine's religious syncretism (Buddhist/Turkic shamanic) is compressed into a single image.
5. "廉颇老矣，尚能饭否" — the allusion to Lian Po (who proved his fitness by eating a peck of rice) can read as self-pity, self-confidence, or bitter irony; the translation leaves the tone open."}

— Xin Qiji

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—where
Is the hero's like? Where is Zhongmou, Sun Quan?
Terraces for song and dance, all elegance and grace,
Swept away by wind and rain without a trace.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
Men say the place once sheltered Ju Nu's domain.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjuxu,
Won them a panicked backward view.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my sight,
The beacon fires of Yangzhou Road burn bright.
How can I bear to look back? At Foli's shrine,
Crows of the gods, drums of the village rite align.
Who will ask if Lian Po, though old, has yet
The strength to eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Ages of mountains and rivers, where heroes once roamed—
No trace remains of Sun Zhongmou.

The pavilions where songs once echoed, the stages where elegance flourished—
All have vanished, swept by wind and rain.

Sunset glimmers through grass and trees, in lanes long known,
Where people say Li Tu once lived.

Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, seeking glory at Langjuxu—
Only to flee in panic, fearing northern pursuit.

Forty-three years pass; still vivid in memory—
The flames blazing along the road to Yangzhou.

How bitter to look back now—
At the temple of Fuli, crows screaming, drums thundering,
Divine chaos in the village.

Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo, still strong enough to eat?"}

A thousand years of rivers and hills—
no hero found where Sun Zhongmou once strode.
Terrace of dance, platform of song,
their elegance all washed away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
in some ordinary lane,
they say the place where Jinu once lived.
Think of those days—
golden spears, iron-shod steeds,
a breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed its campaigns,
seeking to seal the Wolf on Juxu's peak,
and gained only a frantic glance northward.
Forty-three years on,
in the distance I still remember
the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath Foli's shrine,
crows of the gods and drums of the village rites.
Who will ask—
Lan Po is old—
can he still eat his fill?"}

The terraces of dance and song, their elegance forever swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and streets, folk say Jiwu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron steeds, a spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Immortal hills and rivers, here and now,
But no hero to be found, not even like Sun Zhongmu's worth.
Terraces of dance and song, their elegance all gone,
Swept by wind and rain from the world they shone.

The setting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
They say the warlord Liu Yu once lived in these retreats.
Recall those days of golden spears and armored steeds,
A tiger's breath that swallowed ten thousand miles of deeds.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjun in fame,
Won only a panicked glance back north, a hollow claim.
Forty-three years gone by, I still recall the sight,
Of beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou in the night.

How could I bear to look again? At the shrine of Foli,
Crows of the gods and drums of rites, a raucous show.
Who will ask of me now, as Lian Po, who is old,
Can he still eat enough, to be of use should war unfold?"}

The rivers and hills of ages past,
Where heroes like Sun Zhongmou are nowhere to be found.
Dance pavilions and song terraces—
All their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, withered trees, on ordinary lanes,
They say the abode of Ji'nu once stood here.
Think of those days—golden spears and iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yet in Yuanjia, haste and recklessness,
To claim the wolf-slaying merit at Langjuxu,
Only won a panicked glance back northward.
Forty-three years, gazing from afar, I still remember
The beacon fires blazing across Yangzhou's roads.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Foli Shrine, crows and festival drums fill the air.
By who shall it be asked—
Is old Lian Po still able to eat his fill?

2. 原文：舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
   译文：Dance pavilions and song terraces— / All their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
   依据："风流"译为 elegance，兼顾风度与繁华之意；"雨打风吹去"意译为 swept away by wind and rain。

3. 原文：斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
   译文：Slanting sun, withered trees, on ordinary lanes, / They say the abode of Ji'nu once stood here.
   依据："人道"译为 They say，保留传闻语气；"曾住"译为 once stood here。

4. 原文：想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
   译文：Think of those days—golden spears and iron-clad horses, / A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
   依据："气吞"译为 a spirit that swallowed，保留夸张意象；"如虎"直译 like a tiger。

5. 原文：元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
   译文：Yet in Yuanjia, haste and recklessness, / To claim the wolf-slaying merit at Langjuxu, / Only won a panicked glance back northward.
   依据："封狼居胥"典出霍去病，译为 the wolf-slaying merit at Langjuxu，加注地点；"仓皇北顾"译为 a panicked glance back northward。

6. 原文：四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
   译文：Forty-three years, gazing from afar, I still remember / The beacon fires blazing across Yangzhou's roads.
   依据："望中犹记"译为 gazing from afar, I still remember，主语补出为 I。

7. 原文：可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
   译文：How can one bear to look back? / Beneath the Foli Shrine, crows and festival drums fill the air.
   依据："佛狸"音译为 Foli；"神鸦社鼓"译为 crows and festival drums，保留民俗意象，讽刺意味隐含。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: At Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou, Recalling Antiquity

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—
No hero left to find, where once was Sun Zhongmu.
The terraces for dance, the stages for song,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
Men say the place once home to Jinu.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed to war, to seal a wolf on Mount Juxu,
And won only a panicked glance behind.
Forty-three years, and in my gaze I still remember,
Beacon fires blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How could one turn to look again—
At Foli’s shrine, where crows of the gods
And the drums of the village feast fill the air?

Who is there to ask:
Is old Lian Po,
Still able to eat his fill?"}

A thousand ages, this river and these hills—
Where now can one find the hero Sun Zhongmou?
The terraces of song and dance, the elegance of old,
All swept away by wind and rain, beyond recall.
Beneath the slanting sun, on grassy lanes and trees,
In common streets and alleys, men still say
That Liu Yu once dwelt here.
Think of those years—bronze spears, iron-clad steeds,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li, fierce as a tiger.
Yet Yuanjia rushed its campaign,
Seeking honors like those won at Wolf-tower Peak,
Only to flee in panic, glancing northward in dismay.
Forty-three years have passed—
Gazing from here, I still remember
The beacon fires blazing across Yangzhou’s roads.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli, the Northern Wei’s barbarian king,
A flock of crows and the beating of festival drums.
Who will ask, as was asked of Lian Po—
"Is the old man past his prime?
Can he still eat his fill, and fight?""}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy at the Northern Terrace of Jingkou, Recalling the Past

By Xin Qiji

The rivers and hills of a thousand ages—
no place to find the hero Sun Zhongmou.
The terraces of song and dance,
all their elegance, beaten away by wind and rain.
Beneath slanting sun, grass and trees,
in an ordinary lane, they say once lived Ji Nu.
Think of those years—golden spears, iron cavalry—
spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia's haste, to bestow the title 'Wolf Mount,'
gained only a panicked glance to the north.
Forty-three years,
gazing, I still remember the beacon fires of Yangzhou Road.
How can one bear to look back?
At the shrine of Foli,
crows and drums of the spring festival.
Who will ask:
'Lian Po is old—
can he still eat his rice?'

Notes on ambiguities in the original:
1. "孙仲谋处" (Sun Zhongmou chu): "place of Sun Zhongmou" or "where Sun Zhongmou was". Both convey absence.
2. "寄奴" (Ji Nu): nickname of Liu Yu (founder of Liu Song dynasty), literally 'sent slave'.
3. "封狼居胥" (feng Lang Ju Xu): 'to bestow [the title of victory at] Wolf Mount' (alluding to Huo Qubing's victory). Some read it as 'to seal/conquer Langju and Xushan'.
4. "赢得" (ying de): ironically 'gain', here meaning 'ended up with'.
5. "神鸦社鼓" (shen ya she gu): 'shrine crows and festival drums'—vivid but multi-layered: crows feeding at sacrifices, drums of village festivals.}"}

By Xin Qiji

Mountains and rivers stand since ancient times,
But the hero — where is Sun Zhongmou to be found?
Dance-halls and singing-platforms,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
An ordinary lane and path —
The people say the house of Ji Nu once stood.
Think of those years: golden spears and iron horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
In the Yuanjia reign, hastily launched,
Aim to 'seal Mount Langju' —
Only to win a panicked glance back north.
Forty-three years have passed;
In my gaze I still remember,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back —
Beneath the Foli Shrine,
A flock of crows and drums for the village festival.
By whom shall I be asked:
'Lian Po is old —
Can he still eat his rice?'"}

A thousand ages this land and river,
No hero to be found
Where once Sun Zhongmou stood.
The dance pavilions and singing terraces,
Their gallantry all swept away
By wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In some ordinary lane,
Men say the slave once lived.
Think of that year—
Golden spears and iron-hoofed steeds,
Breath swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia acted rashly,
To crown Fenglang Peak,
Only to flee northward in panic.
Forty-three years,
In the distance I still remember
The beacon fires on the Yangzhou road.
How can I bear to look back—
Under the Foli Temple,
A flock of crows and the drums of sacrifice.
Who would ask—
Lian Po is old,
Can he still eat his fill?"}

By Xin Qiji

A thousand ages, this river and these hills—
No hero to be found, where once Sun Zhongmou dwelt.
The terraces for dance, the stages for song,
All their grace and splendor swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets—
They say the place where Jinu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia's haste, to 'seal the Wolf Mount,'
Won only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years gone—still I remember, gazing out,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back? Beneath the Foli Shrine,
A flock of crows and the drums of the spring sacrifice.
Who will ask: Is Lian Po old now?
Can he still eat his fill of rice?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: At Beigu Terrace in Jingkou, Recalling the Past

The land of ages stands, but heroes are no more—
Where Sun Zhongmou dwelt.
The dancing pavilions, the singing stages,
Their elegance has all been washed away
By wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In common alleys and lanes,
Men say Jīnú once dwelt.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
Breath swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia acted rashly,
Wished to crown himself at Langjuxu,
Only to gain a hasty northward glance in panic.

Forty-three years have passed—
In my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Fólí Shrine,
Crows of omen and drums of festival fill the air.

Who will ask?
Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat his fill?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy at the Northern Pavilion of Jingkou — Meditations on the Past
By Xin Qiji

A thousand ages, these rivers and mountains — no hero can be found,
Where once was Sun Zhongmou's ground.
Dancing terraces, singing stages, all their glory swept away,
By wind and rain that beat their day.
Beneath the slanting sun, 'mong grass and trees,
In lanes and alleys common as you please,
They say that once the Ju Nu
dwelt within these walls.
Think of those years — golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A spirit that could swallow ten thousand li like tigers in their deeds.

Yuan Jia, hasty in his war,
To 'Feng Langjuxu' as his goal,
Won only a panicked flight, looking back to the north's control.
Forty-three years have passed —
Still in my gaze I remember,
The beacon fires over Yangzhou's land.
How can I bear to turn my head? Below the Foli Shrine's shade,
A flock of crows and drums of festival are all that are displayed.
By whom will it be asked — has Lian Po grown old,
And can he still eat his fill, and worth be told?"

Notes on ambiguities in the original (optional readings):
1. "人道寄奴曾住" — "寄奴" (Ju Nu) is the childhood name of Liu Yu (Liu Jigu), founder of the Liu Song dynasty. The phrase literally means "people say that Ju Nu once lived here." Some readings emphasize the casual, almost dismissive tone of "people say," suggesting the grand past is now reduced to local gossip.
2. "佛狸祠下" — "佛狸" (Foli) is the nickname of Northern Wei Emperor Taiwu (Tuoba Tao), who pursued the Song army to the Yangtze. The shrine, originally built by locals to appease the northern invader, has become a site of folk worship. The irony — a former enemy now honored in a temple — is deliberate, and the translation preserves "Foli Shrine" without explanation in the main text.
3. "廉颇老矣，尚能饭否" — The allusion to general Lian Po of the Warring States period, who in old age protested his fitness by eating heartily, but was slandered by a jealous informant before the king could verify. The rhetorical question "尚能饭否" ("can he still eat his fill?") is a metaphor for Xin Qiji's own desire to serve the country despite his advanced age, and his fear that slander will again prevent him from being believed. The translation keeps the culinary metaphor intact rather than paraphrasing it as "still fit for service."
4. "四十三年" — This may refer to the forty-three years since Xin Qiji led his southern expedition (1162) to the present moment of writing (c. 1205), or to the forty-three years since the Battle of Caishui (1161). The translation simply states "forty-three years have passed" without specifying which event, preserving the ambiguity."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: At the Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou, Recalling the Past

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and hills;
No hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found today.
Dance pavilions and song stages—
Their elegance, lost to the wind and rain that swept them away.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
The people say Lord Jinu once lived here.
Recall those years—
Golden spears, iron horses, a breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

In the Yuanjia era, acting rashly,
To seal the Wolf Mountain—only a hasty, panicked retreat northward.
Forty-three years have passed,
In my gaze, I still remember the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Crows of the temple, drums of the sacrifice—
Who will ask, "Lian Po is old—can he still eat his fill?""}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: At Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou, Recalling Antiquity

Rivers and mountains through the ages—
No hero left to find, where once was Sun Zhongmu.
The pavilions where they danced, the stages where they sang,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.

The setting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
Men say the place once home to Jinu.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia hastened to war, to perform the fengshan rite on Mount Juxu,
And won only a panicked look northward.
Forty-three years, and looking out, I still recall,
Beacon fires blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How could one turn to look again—
At Foli’s shrine, where crows of the gods
And the drums of the village feast fill the air?

Who is there to ask:
Is old Lian Po,
Still strong enough to eat?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou
— Xin Qiji

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—where
Is the hero's like? Where is Zhongmou, Sun Quan?
Terraces for song and dance, all elegance and grace,
Swept away by wind and rain without a trace.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
Men say the place once sheltered Ju Nu's domain.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like fierce steeds.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjuxu,
Won them nothing but a panicked backward view.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my sight,
The beacon fires of Yangzhou Road burn bright.
How can I bear to look back? At Foli's shrine,
Crows of the gods, drums of the village rite align.
Who will ask if Lian Po, though old, has yet
The strength to eat his fill and not forget?"}

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—where
Is the hero's like? Where is Zhongmou, Sun Quan?
Terraces for song and dance, all elegance and grace,
Swept away by wind and rain without a trace.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
Men say the place once sheltered Ju Nu's domain.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like fierce steeds.

The beacon fires of Yangzhou Road burn bright.

Crows of the gods, drums of the village rite align.
Who will ask if Lian Po, though old, has yet
The strength to eat his fill and not forget?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Reflecting on the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and hills—
No hero can be found, like Sun Zhongmou here.
Dancing terraces and singing stages,
The grace of old, all swept away
By wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
They say the home of Liu Yu once stood.
Think of those years—
Golden spears and iron-hooved steeds,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia's rash campaign,
To seal the Wolf Altar at Junji,
Won only a panicked glance to the north.
Forty-three years have passed,
In my gaze I still remember
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
A flock of crows and drums of village sacrifice.
Who will ask—
Like Lian Po, old and grey,
Can he still eat his fill of rice?"}

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Meditations at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

A thousand ages, this river, these peaks—
no hero left to find where Sun Zhongmou stood.
The dance-halls, the singing terraces,
their elegance, all of it, wind and rain have beaten down.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
in some ordinary lane and market street,
the people say that Liu Ji once lived there.
Think of those years—
golden spears, iron-clad horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li, fierce as a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed things,
to seal the wolf on Mount Juxu,
and won only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years on,
still I remember in the distance,
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back—
beneath the Foli shrine,
a flock of temple crows, the drums of the spring sacrifice.

Who will ask, when Lian Po has grown old,
can he still eat his rice?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: At Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou, Recalling Antiquity

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—
No hero left to find, where once was Sun Zhongmu.
The terraces for dance, the stages for song,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
Men say the place once home to Jinu.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed to war, to seal a wolf on Mount Juxu,
And won only a panicked glance behind.
Forty-three years, and in my gaze I still remember,
Beacon fires blazing on the road to Yangzhou.

How could one turn to look again—
At Foli's shrine, where crows of the gods
And the drums of the village feast fill the air?

Who is there to ask:
Is old Lian Po,
Still able to eat his fill?"}

A thousand ages, rivers and mountains—
no hero can be found, where Sun Zhongmou dwelt.
Dance halls and singing terraces,
their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane—
men say, this is where Jinu once lodged.
Think of those years: golden spears and iron-hooved steeds,
such spirit, swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia's rash campaign, seeking to seal the Wolf Altar in triumph,
gained only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years have passed—
still I remember, gazing out, the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Fili Shrine, a flock of crows and drums for the village feast.
Who will ask:
Lian Po is old—
is he still fit to eat his fill and fight?

4. 金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎 → "golden spears and iron-hooved steeds, such spirit, swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger" — 直译意象。
5. 元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾 → "Yuanjia's rash campaign, seeking to seal the Wolf Altar in triumph, gained only a panicked glance back to the north" — 封狼居胥典出霍去病，此处指刘义隆草率北伐；"赢得"在此含反讽，译为gained only。

— Xin Qiji

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—where
Is the hero's like? Where is Sun Quan, the man?
Terraces for song and dance, all elegance and grace,
Swept away by wind and rain without a trace.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
Men say the place once sheltered Ju Nu's domain.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like fierce beasts.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjuxu,
Won them nothing but a panicked backward view.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my sight,
The beacon fires of Yangzhou Road still burn bright.
How can I bear to look back? At Foli's shrine,
Crows feast on offerings, drums beat at the shrine.
Who will ask if Lian Po, though old, has yet
The strength to eat his fill and not forget?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal hills and rivers — no hero can be found,
nowhere the place of Sun Zhongmou.
Dancing terraces, singing platforms —
all their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane —
they say the place where Jinu once lived.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like tigers.
Yuan Jia rushed to war,
wishing to be crowned at Wolf-Enduring Peak —
only to win a panicked flight, glancing back north.
Forty-three years — gazing out, I still remember
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Foli Shrine,
a flock of crows and the drums of spring sacrifice.
Who will ask — is old Lian Po
eat enough, still?"}

no hero left to find where Sun Zhongmou stood.
The dance-halls, the singing terraces,

in some ordinary lane and market street,

a flock of temple crows, the drums of the spring sacrifice.

A thousand ages, this river, these peaks—
no hero left to find where Sun Zhongmou stood.
The dance-halls, the singing terraces,
their elegance, all of it, wind and rain have beaten down.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
in some ordinary lane and market street,
the people say that Liu Ji once lived there.
Think of those years—
golden spears, iron-clad horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li, fierce as a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed things,
to seal the wolf on Mount Juxu,
and won only a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years on,
still I remember in the distance,
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back—
beneath the Foli shrine,
a flock of temple crows, the drums of the spring sacrifice.

Who will ask, when Lian Po has grown old,
can he still eat his rice?}"}

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—where
Is the hero's like? Where is Zhongmou, Sun Quan?
Terraces for song and dance, all elegance and grace,
Swept away by wind and rain without a trace.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
Men say the place once sheltered Ju Nu's domain.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A might like tigers, swallowing ten thousand miles.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjuxu,
Only a panicked retreat, glancing northward in dismay.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my sight,
The beacon fires of Yangzhou Road burn bright.
How can I bear to look back? At the shrine of Foli, the Tartar invader turned god,
Crows of the gods, drums of the village rite align.
Who now will ask: "Is Lian Po old,
And can he still eat well?""}

A thousand ages, this river and these hills—

Dancing pavilions and singing terraces,
all their brilliance, swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,

won them only a frantic glance back in retreat.
Forty-three years have passed—
gazing north even now, I still remember
the beacon fires blazing on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Benei Shrine [temple to the Northern Wei emperor Wuzhi, known as Benei],
where crows of the gods and drums of the village festival fill the air.
Who will ask, as they once asked of Lian Po:

— Xin Qiji

A thousand years of rivers and mountains—where
Is the hero's like? Where is Zhongmou, Sun Quan?
Terraces for song and dance, all elegance and grace,
Swept away by wind and rain without a trace.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
Men say Ju Nu once made his home here.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles, fierce as tigers.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, to seal Mount Langjuxu,
Won them nothing but a panicked backward view.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my gaze I remember,
The beacon fires along Yangzhou Road.
How can I bear to look back? At Foli's shrine,
Crows of the offerings, drums of the village rite,
One scene of noise. Who will ask if Lian Po, though old,
Has yet the strength to eat his fill?"}

A thousand ages, this land of rivers and mountains — no hero can be found, where once Sun Zhongmou stood.
The terraces for dancing and platforms for singing, all their elegance swept away by wind and rain.
Beneath the slanting sun, among grass and trees, on common lanes and streets, they say the home of Jinu once stood.
Think of those years — golden spears and iron-hoofed horses, a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
In the Yuanjia reign, hasty and rash, they sought to seal the wolf on Mount Ju, only to win a panicked glance back to the north.
Forty-three years have passed; gazing afar, I still remember the beacon fires over the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back — beneath the Temple of Foli, a flock of crows and the drums of the spring festival.
Who will ask whether old Lian Po can still eat his fill?"}

At Yujing's Northern Terrace, I remember heroes past—
Sun Zhongmou's might, now nowhere to be found.
The terraces where songs and dances once soared,
All swept away by wind and rain's relentless sound.
Beneath the slanting sun, through grass and trees,
On ordinary lanes, one says Liu Yu once lived.
Imagine those years: halberds gleaming, warhorses strong,
A tiger's breath that swallowed ten thousand miles of land.
Yet Yuanjia's hasty campaign, the wolf-topped peaks a prize,

The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look again—before the Foli Shrine,
Where crows and drumbeats fill the air with offerings profane.
Who can ask if old Lian Po, though aged and gray,
Still has the strength to eat and lead the fray?"}

Ages of rivers and mountains—no hero can be found,
Where once Sun Zhongmou held his ground.
The terraces of song and dance, all glory swept away,\nBy wind and rain that beat upon them, day by day.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane,
They say the home of Liu Yu was there in olden reign.
Think of those years—spear of bronze, steeds of iron mail,
Spirits swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as a gale.

In Yuanjia's haste they sought the wolf-crested hill for fame,
Only to flee in panic, looking back in shame.
Forty-three years have passed—still in my sight I see,
The beacon fires that blazed along Yangzhou's road, for me.
How can I bear to look again at Foli's shrine below,
Where crows circle altars, drums for local gods bestow?

Who will ask me—like Lian Po grown old and gray,
Can he still eat his rice, and fight another day?"}

Across the ages the rivers and mountains remain, yet no hero like Sun Zhongmou can be found.
The terraces of song and dance, all their elegance, beaten away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes and alleys, people say the abode of Jiannu once stood.
Think of those days: golden spears and iron-hooved horses, a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia's rash campaign, to confer the title at Xiongnu's Mount Lang, only earned a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years: in my gaze I still remember the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back, beneath the Temple of Foli, a flock of crows and drums of the village festival.
By whom can I ask: is old Lian Po, though aged, still able to eat his fill?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal mountains and rivers — no hero to be found
where Sun Zhongmou once held sway.

Terraces of song and dance, all that elegance
beaten and scattered by wind and rain.
On a slanting sun through grass and trees, in common lanes and streets,
they say once lived the man called Jinu.
Think of those years: golden spears and iron horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed things — to 'seal the wolf at Mount Ju' —
only to win a panicked glance back north.

Forty-three years on, looking out I still remember
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back —
beneath the shrine of Foli,
a flock of crows and the drums of the spring festival.

Who will ask: is Lian Po old now?
Can he still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal hills and rivers, where no hero may be found—
Sun Quan’s place, long lost.
The pavilions of dance and song, the elegance and brilliance of old,
All washed away by years of wind and rain.

Sunset on grass and trees,
In common alleys, they say Liu Yu once dwelt here.
Recalling those days:
Steel horses, golden spears, a force that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia’s haste, seeking glory at Wolf Juxu,
Only to flee in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed; even now, I see—
The fires of Yangzhou’s route in my mind’s eye.

How bitter to look back—
Beneath the temple of Fuli, crows screech, drums thud for gods.

Who dares ask:
Old General Lianpo—
Is he still fit to serve his country?"}

people say once lived the camp-follower's son.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron horses,
spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia rushed to war, seeking to seal the wolf at Mount Ju;

By Xin Qiji

Across the ages, the rivers and mountains remain—
but no hero can be found where Sun Zhongmou once held sway.
Terraces for dance and song—their elegance
all swept away by wind and rain and weathered gray.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in common lanes,
folk say the place where Liu Yu once stayed.
Think of those years—swords of bronze, steeds in mail,
with the might to swallow ten thousand miles like a tiger's raid.

In Yuanjia, they rushed to glory, aiming to crown wolves on Mount Xue,
only to earn a hasty flight, glancing back in dismay.

Forty-three years gone by—gazing out, I still recall
the beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back? At Foli Shrine,
crows of the gods caw, drums for the village rites sound low.

Who will ask: is Lian Po old, though he still eats his fill with might?

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

No trace of Sun Zhongmou can be found.
On pavilions dancing, in halls singing, all grandeur
Is swept away by rain and wind.
Sunset stains the grass and trees;
In common alleys, they say Liu Yu once lived.
Recalling those days—
With golden spears and iron horses,
He charged with a tiger's might, swallowing ten thousand li.
Yuanjia's haste, his reckless pursuit of glory,
Seizing Mount Laoxu, yet fled in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed—
In memory still: the smoldering fires along the Yangzhou road.
Who can bear to look back?
At the temple of Foli, crows scatter, drums beat in ritual frenzy.
Who dares ask—old General Lianpo?
Is he still able to eat?"}

Recall those days: iron chariots, steel horses, a spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger. 
Yuanjia's campaign was hastily begun; seeking glory at Langju, yet fleeing in panic northward. 
Forty-three years have passed—still vividly remembered, the flames along the Yangzhou road. 
How unbearable to look back: at Fuli’s temple, crows screeching, drums beating for the village gods.

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Land, Eternal Hills — no hero may be found
where once Sun Zhongmou held the ground.
Dancing terraces, singing halls, their splendor all
downpours and winds have beaten into fall.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, an ordinary lane —
they say here once the commoner Liu Yuan lived his reign.
How fierce they were in years gone by: golden halberds, iron steeds,
a tiger's might that swallowed ten thousand miles of deeds.

Yuanjia rushed to war, sought honors like Feng Quxu's stone, and won
only a panicked glance back north, a rout, a fall undone.
Forty-three years have passed; in the view I still recall
the beacon fires that blazed along Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look again — beneath the Fox Spirit shrine,
crows croaking, drums of village rite, a pagan sign.
Who will ask now: is old Lian Po, though gray and worn,
yet able still to eat his fill of corn?\n
\n[Note on the original phrase \"元嘉草草，封狼居胥\" : \"草草\" may read as \"hastily, rashly\" (the Yuanjia campaigns were launched in haste) or as \"carelessly, without due preparation\"; both senses are retained in \"rushed to war\". \"佛狸\" is the Xianbei emperor Tuoba Tao, whose shrine later stood on the northern bank of the Yangtze.]"}

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

A thousand autumns, rivers and hills—
No hero left where Sun Zhongmou stood.
Dance-halls and song-screens,
All their elegance swept off by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In lanes and streets of common fame—
They say here General Jinu once dwelt.
Think of those days: golden spears, iron steeds,
A breath that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia rushed headlong,
To seal the Wolf on Mount Juxu,
But won only a hasty glance north in flight.

Forty-three years have passed—
Still I recall, in all I see,
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How could I turn my head?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Crows croak, and temple drums beat.

Who will ask: Lian Po is old—
Can he still eat his fill of rice?"}

Recalling those days: golden spears, iron horses, spirit devouring a thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia, hasty and ill-prepared, sought to seal the Wolf's Ridge, yet fled in panic northward.

By Xin Qiji

For ages, this landscape of rivers and mountains endures,
Yet no hero is found—no trace of Sun Zhongmou's towers.
Those terraces of song and dance, those graceful displays,
All swept away by wind and rain, lost in bygone days.

Beneath the slanting sun, among grass and common trees,
In lanes and streets unknown, they say once lived Liu Yu with ease.
Recall those years—his armored host, his steeds of war,
Like a tiger, his spirit devoured ten thousand miles afar.

Only to flee in panic, casting fearful glances toward the northern flight.
Forty-three years have passed, and still before my eyes
The beacon fires over Yangzhou's roads in memory rise.

How can I bear to look back? Beneath the Foli temple's shade,
Only crows swoop and drums resound for the barbarian god they parade.
Who will ask now—like Lian Po, grown old and gray,
Can he still fight, though appetite remains, this very day?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

No trace of Sun Zhongmou can be found.
On pavilions dancing, in halls singing, all grandeur
Is swept away by rain and wind.
Dim sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
They say Li Mu once lived here.
I recall those days: golden spears and iron horses,
A spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia rashly rushed, seeking to conquer the Wolf Ridge,
Only to flee in panic, looking back northward.
Forty-three years have passed; still, in memory,
I see flames lighting up the road to Yangzhou.
How painful to look back—
At the temple of Fu Li, crows flying, drums beating, gods and ghosts in frenzy.
Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo, is he still strong enough to eat?"}

Sunset among grass and trees, ordinary alleys where people say Li Nu once lived.
Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses, a spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign, sealing the wolf at Juxu, yet only panic fleeing north in haste.
Forty-three years have passed; even now I see clearly—the fires of war along the Yangzhou road.
How unbearable it is to look back: at the temple of Foli, crows soaring, drums for the spring festival echoing.

In lanes so common, they say Liu Yu lived before.
Recall those days: steel horses charging, war cries loud,
A might that swallowed vast lands like a tiger in its proud.

Sought to enshrine fame on the Wolf's Ridge high—

Forty-three years pass, yet in memory's gaze,

Crows cry, drums beat—worshipers' fervor all around.
Who dares ask now—old General Lianpo, though aged,
Can he still eat his meals? Still strong, still brave, unswayed?"}

Yuanjia's hasty campaign, chasing glory at Langjuxu, only left panic as he fled northward.

Yuanjia's hasty campaign, sealing the wolf at Juxu, only left frantic retreats northward.

the place of Sun Zhongmou.

Dancing terraces, singing platforms,
all their elegance swept away
by wind and rain.

Slanting sun, grass and trees,
an ordinary lane and street—
they say Jigu once lived here.

Think of those years:
golden spears, iron-hooved horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

In the Yuanjia reign, rashly,
they sought to seal off Mount Langju,
only to win a hurried retreat, glancing north in alarm.

Forty-three years have passed—
looking out, I still remember
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.

How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
only crows and the drums of the spring festival.

By whom will it be asked:
Lian Po is old—
can he still eat his fill?"}

Recall those days: golden spears clashing, iron horses charging—mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.
Yuanjia's reckless haste, sealing the wolf at Juxu, only to flee in panic northward.
Forty-three years pass; still vivid in memory—the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.

Palaces of dance and song, grandeur once so bright,
Now all washed away by wind and rain.
Sunset among grass and trees, in humble alleys,
They say Li Ju once lived here.
I recall those days: golden weapons, iron horses,
A spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's rash campaign, sealing the wolf at Juxu,
Only left frantic retreats northward.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in memory,
The flames along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable to look back—
At Buddha's Temple, crows fly, drums sound, a godly noise.
Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo, can he still eat?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal rivers and mountains, heroes sought in vain—
Where once stood Sun Zhongmou.
The pavilions where songs once soared, the stages where elegance reigned,
All have long since been swept by wind and rain.

Sunset glows on grass and trees,
In lanes and alleys ordinary as ever—
They say Li Tu lived here.
Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

But Emperor Yuanjia’s haste,
Seizing Mount Langju,
Only brought frantic retreat and fearful glances north.

Forty-three years pass in thought—
Still vivid in memory:
Fires blazing along the road to Yangzhou.

How unbearable to look back—
At Buddha's Temple, crows screaming, drums thundering,
A chaos of gods and folk.

Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo—
Can he still eat his meal?"}

Where once stood Sun Zhongmou.
The pavilions where songs once soared, the stages where elegance reigned,
All have long since been swept by wind and rain.

Sunset glows on grass and trees,
In lanes and alleys ordinary as ever—
They say Li Tu lived here.
Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses,
Mighty as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.

But Emperor Yuanjia’s haste,
Seizing Mount Langju,
Only brought frantic retreat and fearful glances north.

Forty-three years pass in thought—
Still vivid in memory:
Fires blazing along the road to Yangzhou.

How unbearable to look back—
At Buddha's Temple, crows screaming, drums thundering,
A chaos of gods and folk.

Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo—
Can he still eat his meal?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Palaces of dance and halls of song, all grandeur swept away by rain and wind.
Sunset among grass and trees, ordinary lanes and alleys where people say Li Nu once lived.
Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses, roaring like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.
Yuanjia rashly, seeking glory at Langjuxu, only to flee in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in sight—the fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How bitter to look back—on the temple of Foli, crows flying, drums beating in solemn rites.
Who dares ask? Old General Lian Po—still able to eat his meal?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal mountains and rivers—
No trace of heroes remains,
No place of Sun Zhongmou.
Dancing terraces and singing platforms,
All their splendor swept away
By wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In an ordinary lane,
They say the residence of Jinu stood here.
Think of those years—
Golden spears, iron-hooved steeds,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
In the Yuanjia reign, hasty campaigns,
To confer the title at Langjuxu,
Only earned a panicked retreat, glancing northward.
Forty-three years have passed,
Gazing from here, I still remember
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?
At the foot of the Foli Shrine,
A flock of crows and the drums of spring festival.
Who will ask:
"Is Lian Po too old?
Can he still eat his fill?""}

Recalling those days: golden spears clashing, iron horses thundering—ambition devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia hastily marched, seeking glory at Langju, only to flee in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed; in memory still, flames blaze along the road to Yangzhou.

Think of those years: golden spears and iron-clad horses, a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia's rash campaign, to bestow the title of Wolf-Treading Marshal,

Forty-three years, gazing afar I still remember—the beacon fires over Yangzhou Road.

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。

Scaffolds for dancing, stages for song, all elegance now battered by wind and rain.
Sunset among grass and trees, in ordinary alleys, they say Liu Yuzu lived here.
Recall those days: golden spears and iron horses, a spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia, hasty and reckless, seeking glory at Longju, only to flee in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed; even now I see in mind the fires along the Yangzhou road.
Unbearable to turn back—the temple of Fuli, crows flying, drums beating in sacred frenzy.
Who dares ask? Old General Lianpo—still able to eat his meal?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

where Sun Zhongmu once ruled.
The terraces of song and dance,
all their elegance, swept away
by wind and rain.
On setting sun and grassy trees,
in common lanes and streets —
they say the place where Jinu once lived.
Think of those years:
bronze spears and iron horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia rushed into battle,
hoping to carve a record at Wolf-tail Peak,
and won only a panicked glance northward.
Forty-three years,
gazing out I still remember
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back —
beneath the shrine of Foli,
the crows of the altar and the drums of the festival.
Who will ask:
Lian Po is old —
can he still eat his fill?"}

舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal rivers and mountains — nowhere can one find
the hero Sun Zhongmou now.
Dance pavilions and singing terraces, all that elegance, is swept away
by wind and driving rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in an ordinary lane —
so people say, that is where the warlord Liu Yu once lived.
Think of those years: bronze halberds and iron-hoofed horses,
a spirit that swallowed ten thousand miles, fierce as a tiger.
Yet Yuanjia rushed its campaign, seeking to seal the Wolf-tower on Mount Ju,
only to earn a panicked flight, looking back in fear.
Forty-three years have passed, and gazing out I still remember
the beacon fires blazing along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back —
beneath the shrine of Foli, crows of the gods and drums of the village festival?
Who will ask, now that Lian Po is old,
whether he can still eat his fill of rice?"}

I recall those days: golden spears and iron horses, a spirit devouring thousands of miles like a tiger.

Sunset among grass and trees, in humble lanes where people say Liu Yu once lived.
Recalling those days: golden spears and iron horses, breathing fierce as a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.
Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, seeking to seal the wolf at Juxu, ended only in frantic retreat northward.
Forty-three years have passed; even now, I still recall the fires along the road to Yangzhou.
How bitter to look back—beneath the altar of Emperor Foli, crows cry and drums sound for the village gods.
Who dares ask—Lian Po is old, but can he still eat?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Where once Sun Zhongmou held his ground.
Dance pavilions, singing terraces—all that grace
Swept away by wind and rain, without a trace.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes and streets so plain,
They say Jinu once lived here in his reign.
Think of that year: golden spears, iron-hoofed steeds,
A fury swallowing ten thousand li, like a tiger's deeds.

Yuanjia's hasty venture, crowning Langjuxu's height,
Won only a panicked glance northward in flight.
Forty-three years have passed—still I recall,
The beacon fires blazing over Yangzhou's road.
How can I bear to look back? Beneath Foli's shrine,
Crows and festival drums in a desolate line.
Who will ask: is Lian Po old, can he still eat?"}

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

no trace of heroes, not even Sun Zhongmou.
The terraces of song and dance,
all their glory washed away by wind and rain.
Beneath the slanting sun, grass and trees,
in common lanes and alleys,
they say the house of Jinu once stood.
Think of those years—
iron cavalry, golden spears,
whose breath swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's haste,
to seal Mount Lang,
won only a panicked glance to the north.
Forty-three years,
gazing from here I still remember
the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
crows and festival drums.
Who will ask—
like Lian Po, old now,
can he still eat his fill?"}

Thinking back then: golden spears and iron horses, a spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's campaign was hastily begun; seeking to seal the wolf at Juxu, only to flee in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed; in my memory still burns the fire along the road to Yangzhou.
How painful to look back—the temple of Fuli, filled with crows' cries and drums of worship.

舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "For ages the rivers and mountains stand; no hero can be found—
Sun Zhongmou's place.
Dance-halls and singing terraces, all their elegance,
beaten and blown away by wind and rain.
Beneath slanting sun, among grass and trees, in common lanes,
people say once Jigu dwelt.
Think of those years—bronze spears and iron-clad horses,
a spirit swallowing ten thousand li, like a tiger.
Yuanjia's heedless campaign, to confer the title at Langjuxu,
won only a hurried retreat, glancing back north.
Forty-three years on, in the distance I still remember
the beacon fires over Yangzhou road.
How can one bear to look back?—
Beneath Foli Shrine, a flock of crows and drums of the spring sacrifice.
On whom can one ask—
is Lian Po old? Can he still eat his fill?"}

A thousand ages, these rivers and lands—
No hero to be found now, where Sun Zhongmou once reigned.
The terraces of dance, the stages of song,
All elegance swept away at last by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes and streets so plain—
People say that Jigu once lived here, too.
Think of those years: gold-tipped spears, ironclad steeds,
A spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.
Yuanjia rushed to war, hoping to seal honors at Langjuxu,
Only to earn a panicked glance backward, fleeing north.
Forty-three years—and still in my gaze I remember,
The beacon-fires blazed along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back? At the Foxi Shrine,
A flock of crows and drums for the village feast.
Who will ask whether Lian Po, now old,

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

Palaces of dance and songs, grandeur that once was, all swept away by rain and wind.
Sunset stains the grass and trees; in these common alleys, people say Liu Yu once lived here.
Thinking back then: golden armor, iron horses, a spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's campaign was hasty; he sought to seal the wolf at Juxu, only to flee in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed—the scene still recalls, in sight, the warfare across Yangzhou’s roads.
How unbearable to look back now: beneath the temple of Foli, crows cry, and village drums sound in reverence.
Who will ask—Lian Po is old, but can he still eat?"}

Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses, a spirit devouring ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, sealing the mountain Wolf Juxu, yet ended in frantic retreat northward.

Recall those days: golden swords clashing, iron horses galloping, breath like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles.
Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, seeking glory at Langjuxu, only left frantic retreats northward.

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

The pavilions of dance and song, the elegance once lived, now battered by wind and rain. 
Sunset lights the grass and trees; in these common alleys, they say Liu Yu once dwelled. 
Recall those days: armored horses, iron spears, a spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger. 

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, sealing the wolf at Juxu—only to flee north in panic. 
Forty-three years have passed; I still remember clearly the fires on the road to Yangzhou. 
How bitter to look back—where the temple of Foli stands, crows cry, drums beat for the gods! 
Who dares ask—though old General Lianpo may be frail, can he still eat?"}

Recall those days: armored horses, iron spears, a spirit that devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger. 

Yuanjia’s hasty campaign, sealing the wolf at Juxu—only to flee north in panic. 
Forty-three years have passed; I still remember clearly the fires on the road to Yangzhou. 
How bitter to look back—where the temple of Foli stands, crows cry, drums beat for the gods! 
Who dares ask—though old General Lianpo may be frail, can he still eat?"}

I recall those days—armored horses and iron swords, a force that swallowed ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign, seeking glory at Langjuxu, only brought frantic retreats northward.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in mind—the fires along the Yangzhou road.
How unbearable to look back—Bolí Temple, where crows cry and drums sound in reverence.

But where shall one find the place of Sun Zhongmou?
Terraces where dancers swayed, stages where singers rang—
Their splendor all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes both plain and common,
The people say: here once lived Ji Nu.
Recall those years of iron spears and armored steeds,
A tiger's breath that swallowed ten thousand li.
Yuan Jia rushed to war, his aim to seal the Wolf mountain,
Yet gained nothing but panic, glancing north in flight.
Forty-three years have passed—before my eyes
I still recall the beacon fires of Yangzhou's roads.
How can one bear to look back now?
Beneath the shrine of Foli, spirit crows gather
Over a shrine where village drums resound.
Who will ask me, aging Lian Po—
Is he still able to eat his fill?"}

舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。

元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "The eternal rivers and mountains remain,
But where shall one find a hero like Sun Zhongmou?
Terraces where dancers swayed, stages where singers rang—
Their splendor all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes both plain and common,
The old folk tell how here once Ji Nu dwelt.
Recall those years of iron spears and armored steeds,
A tiger's breath that swallowed ten thousand li.
Yuan Jia rushed to war, his aim to seal the Wolf mountain,
Yet won but panic-stricken northward glances.
Forty-three years have passed—before my eyes
I still recall the beacon fires of Yangzhou's roads.
How can one bear to look back now?
Beneath the shrine of Foli, the spirit crows
Peck at offerings while drums of village rites resound.
Who will ask me, aging Lian Po—
Can you still eat your fill?"}

But where shall one find a hero like Sun Zhongmou?
Terraces where dancers swayed, stages where singers rang—
Their splendor all swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes both plain and common,
The people say: here once lived Ji Nu.
Recall those years of iron spears and armored steeds,
A tiger's breath that swallowed ten thousand li.
Yuan Jia rushed to war, his aim to seal the Wolf mountain,
Yet won but panic-stricken northward glances.
Forty-three years have passed—before my eyes
I still recall the beacon fires of Yangzhou's roads.
How can one bear to look back now?
Beneath the shrine of Foli, the spirit crows
Peck at offerings while drums of village rites resound.
Who will ask me, aging Lian Po—
Can you still eat your fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "The river and the hills remain, but where
Is the great champion, Sun Zhongmou? None can find.
The dancing terraces, the singing stages—all
Their elegance is swept away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun on grass and trees, in lanes and streets
Ordinary, they say it was where Jinu lived.
Then, how the iron-shod horses and the gleaming spears
Did swallow ten thousand miles, a tiger's breath!
Yuanjia, rash and hasty, sought to seal the wolf on Lüju,
But won only a panicked glance to the north.
Forty-three years have passed, and still from this height
I see the beacon fires of the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back? Beneath the Fuli shrine,
The sacred crows and drums of the village festival.
Who will ask me now, like Lian Po grown old,
If I can still eat?"}

Recalling those days, golden spears and iron horses, his spirit swallowed the world like a tiger.
Yuanjia, hasty and unprepared, seeking to seal the wolf at Juxu, only gained frantic retreat to the north.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in memory, the fires along the Yangzhou road.
How painful it is to look back—where the temple of Fuli stands, crows feast, and drums beat for the village gods.

On the dancing pavilions and singing terraces,
All glory has been swept away by wind and rain.

They say Liu Yu once lived here.
I recall those days: golden spears and iron horses,
Like a tiger devouring ten thousand miles with might.
Yuanjia's campaign was hasty and ill-planned,
Seizing Mount Lianxu, yet fleeing in panic northward.
Forty-three years have passed; still vivid in memory,
The flames along the road to Yangzhou.
How unbearable to look back:
At the temple of Fu Li, crows fly, drums beat in prayer.
Who dares ask: Old General Lianpo—is he still able to eat?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。

No trace of Sun Zhongmou can be found.
On pavilions dancing, stages singing, all that grace
Is battered by rain and wind, swept away by time.
Sunset through grass and trees, in lanes of common folk,
They say Li Tu once lived here.
Recall those days: golden spears, iron horses, 
A spirit so fierce it devoured ten thousand miles like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign, seeking glory on Mount Lian, 
Ended in panic, fleeing northward in haste.
Forty-three years have passed—still vivid in mind:
Fires blazing along the road to Yangzhou.
How bitter to look back—
At the Temple of Fo-li, crows cawing, drums thumping in worship.
Who will ask: Old General Lianpo—can he still eat?"}

Where Sun Zhongmou once stood—no hero found. 
Pavilions of dance, halls of song, 
Washed away by rain and wind, long gone. 

Sunset among grass and trees, 
In common alleys where people say 
Ji Lu once lived— 
Recall those days: golden weapons, iron horses, 
Swallowing ten thousand li whole like a tiger. 

Hastily in Yuanjia, 
To seal the Wolf’s Ridge— 
Only to flee northward in panic. 
Forty-three years passed, 
Still in sight, the fires along the Yangzhou route. 

Dare one look back? 
Beneath the Temple of Foli, 
Sacred crows, village drums. 
Who dares ask: 
Is General Lianpo old? Can he still eat?"}
