乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "**The River Chant: Reflections at Red Cliff**
*To the tune of Niannu Jiao — by Su Shi*

The great river rolls eastward, its waves
washing away a thousand years of heroes.
West of the old ramparts, they say, lies
Red Cliff—where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms once stood.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky; startled waves
crash upon the shore, hurling up
heaps of snow-white foam.
The land and river, like a painting—
how many bold souls once thronged this place.

I think back to Gongjin in his prime,
when Xiao Qiao had just become his bride—
so valorous, so magnificent in bearing.
Feather fan and silken headcloth, amid
easy talk and laughter, the enemy's
masts and hulls turned to ash and drifting smoke.

My spirit wanders to that vanished kingdom.
Those who love me would surely laugh
to see my temples already silvered.
This world is but a dream—
so let me pour one cup of wine
to the river and the moon."}

We gazed at each other, wordless,

I know each year the place that breaks my heart:

Ten years apart, life and death, each lost in endless haze—
I try not to think of you, yet cannot forget.
Your lonely grave lies a thousand miles away;
nowhere to pour out all this grief.
Even if we met, you would not know me now:
dust upon my face, temples white as frost.

Last night a haunting dream brought me home again—
by the small window, you were combing your hair.

Where can I speak of this desolation?

Even if we met, you would not know me,
My face covered in dust, my temples like frost.

Last night, in a quiet dream, I suddenly returned to our hometown.
By the small window, you were combing your hair and putting on your make-up.

We gazed at each other, speechless,
With only a thousand lines of tears.

I know that year after year, where my heart will break,
Is on the moonlit night, at the small pine-covered hill."}

{"source": {"title": "蝶恋花·伫倚危楼风细细", "author": "柳永", "text": "伫倚危楼风细细，望极春愁，黯黯生天际。
草色烟光残照里，无言谁会凭阑意。
拟把疏狂图一醉，对酒当歌，强乐还无味。
衣带渐宽终不悔，为伊消得人憔悴。"}, "translation": "**A Love of Butterflies: Standing by the Tower**

Leaning long against the high tower in the soft breeze,
I gaze till spring's sorrow rises darkly from the sky's edge.
In the fading light, grass and misty hues blend at dusk—
Silent, who could understand the feeling of leaning on the rail?

I mean to cast off restraint and drink myself drunk,
Sing with wine before me, yet forced merriment has no taste at all.
My clothes grow wider day by day, yet I do not repent—
For her sake, I am content to waste away."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "**To the Tune of *Niannujiao*: Reflections at Red Cliff**

The Great River flows east, its waves washing away
The heroes of a thousand ages, gone in spray.

West of the ancient ramparts, so the tale has run,
Stands the Red Cliff where Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms won.

Rugged rocks pierce the sky, waves crash upon the shore,
And roll up a thousand heaps of snow-white spray once more.

The land is a painting; how many heroes then
Were fired with valor on this stage of fighting men.

I think of Zhou Yu then, when Xiaoqiao was his bride,
In youthful splendor, with his martial pride.

A feather fan, a silk cap on his head,
He smiled and talked, and enemy ships lay dead.

My soul wanders the realm of old; if passion's flow
Made me laugh at myself for white hair, years ago.

But life is but a dream; I toast the moon's reflection here,
And pour this cup of wine to the river, without fear."}

The wind has settled; dust still bears the flower's scent—all blooms are spent.
The day grows late; too weary now to comb my hair.
Things stay the same, yet all the people I have lost—
every thing is done. I would speak, but tears flow first.

I've heard that spring at Double Creek is still fair,
so I meant to drift there in a light boat—
only I fear those slender zhemeng boats
could never carry such a heavy load of sorrow."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "# Reflections on the Past at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Eternal rivers, eternal hills — no hero here remains to find,
Nor where once Sun Quan ruled, lord of these plain-swept lands and skies.
Dance halls and song pavilions, grace and glory, all
Are borne away by wind and rain's unceasing fall.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
People say the servant-boy once dwelt within these frames.
Recall that year: golden spears, iron-armored steeds at war,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand li, fierce as tiger's roar.

The Yuanjia emperor, rash and overbold, pressed north to seal
The wolf on Xue Mountain's peak — won but a panicked flight, a backward steal
At the foe's pursuit. Forty-three years have flown, and still I see
The beacon fires that blazed the road toward Yangzhou's plains and sea.

How can one bear to turn one's gaze to what has been —
Beneath Foli's shrine, the crows squawking, the drumbeats' din?
Who now will ask me: "Is the old Lian Po past his prime?
Can he still eat, though winter's here upon his time?""}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows eastward, its waves washing away
The heroes of a thousand ages, swept and gone.
West of the old ramparts, men say, lies
The Red Cliff of the Three Kingdoms, where young Zhou Yu shone.
Jagged rocks pierce the void, fierce waves crash the shore,
And roll up a thousand heaps of white foam.
The land is like a painting,
How many heroes of that time were born!

I think of Gongjin in his youthful years,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, his heroic spirit shone.
With a feather fan and a silk cap, as he talked and laughed,
The enemy's masts and hulls were turned to ashes and smoke, and were gone.
My spirit wanders to that ancient land,
The sentimental one should laugh at me, for my hair has turned to white so soon.
The world is but a dream,
I pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "江城子·乙卯正月二十日夜记梦", "author": "苏轼", "text": "十年生死两茫茫，不思量，自难忘。
千里孤坟，无处话凄凉。
纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜。
夜来幽梦忽还乡，小轩窗，正梳妆。
相顾无言，惟有泪千行。
料得年年肠断处，明月夜，短松冈。"}, "translation": "**A Dream on the Night of the Twentieth Day of the First Month, Year Yi-mao**

Ten years, dead and alive, a boundless haze—
I never dwell on you, yet I never cease to recall.
A thousand miles away, a lonely grave;
nowhere to speak of this desolation.

Even should we meet again, you would not know me—
my face all dust, my temples frosted white.

Last night, a dim dream carried me home again—
by the small lattice window, you were dressing your hair.
Our eyes met; neither spoke.
Only tears, ten thousand lines of them.

I know the place where year after year my heart breaks:
a night of bright moon, on the short-pine hill."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "# Nian Nu Jiao: Reflections at Red Cliff
*Su Shi*

The great river rolls east, its surging waves
Washing away the heroes bold
Of all the ages past.

West of the old ramparts, so they say,
Is Red Cliff—where young Zhou Yu fought
In the Three Kingdoms' fray.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves
Crash on the shore, rolling up
A thousand crests of white like foam and spray.

The land and river, like a painting bright—
How many heroes flourished in that age of light!

I dream of Gongjin in his years of prime,
When Xiao Qiao was freshly wed—
His bearing bold, his spirit sublime.

A feather fan, a silken cap, at ease,
He laughed and talked—and enemy masts and hulls
Were ground to ash, dissolved like smoke on the breeze.

My spirit soars to that ancient land;
The sentimental would laugh to see
My temples graying—I understand.

This world is but a dream, a fleeting breath—
One cup I pour to the river and the moon's soft beam."}

*Su Shi*

Ten years between life and death — all blurred and vast.
I don't dwell on you, yet never have I forgotten.
A lonely grave a thousand miles away;
nowhere to speak of this desolate chill.

Even if we met again, you would not know me —
face caked with dust, temples frosted white.

Last night a hushed dream carried me home:
the small lattice window, you at your mirror,
combing your hair.

We gazed at each other, wordless;
only a thousand lines of tears.

I know where, year after year, my heart will break —
on moonlit nights, by the low pine-covered mound."}

A thousand miles away stands the lonely grave,

Even if we met again, you would not know me —
my face grimed with dust, my temples frosted white.

By the small windowed pavilion you were at your toilet.
We gazed at each other, speechless,

I know, year after year, the place where hearts are broken:

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "**Nian Nu Jiao: Reflections at Red Cliff**

The Great River runs eastward,
its waves washing away
a thousand ages of brilliant men.

West of the old ramparts,
they say, stood Zhou Yu's Red Cliff
of the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks split the sky, fierce waves
crash on the shore, rolling up
a thousand heaps of snow.

The land, a painting—
how many heroes thronged that time!

I think back to Gongjin in his youth,
Xiao Qiao newly wed,
a presence proud and bright.
Feather fan and silken cap—
in talk and laughter,
enemy masts and hulls
were blown to ash and smoke.

My soul roams the ancient kingdom's ground:
if moved, I should be laughed at
for graying hair come too soon.

All life is but a dream—
I pour a cup to the river and moon."}

I think to cast off restraint and seek just one drunken hour,

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

have washed away the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old battlements, they say,
was the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
startling waves crash the shore,
piling up ten thousand drifts of snow.
The land and river are like a painting,
so many heroes in their prime.

I think back to Gongjin in his youth,
just married to Xiao Qiao,
his heroic bearing and brilliant spirit.
With a feather fan and silk cap,
in talk and laughter, the enemy's masts
turned to ash and smoke.
My soul wanders to that ancient kingdom,
and the passionate should laugh at me
for my early graying hair.
The human world is but a dream;
I pour a cup to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "江城子·乙卯正月二十日夜记梦", "author": "苏轼", "text": "十年生死两茫茫，不思量，自难忘。
千里孤坟，无处话凄凉。
纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜。
夜来幽梦忽还乡，小轩窗，正梳妆。
相顾无言，惟有泪千行。
料得年年肠断处，明月夜，短松冈。"}, "translation": "**Jiangchengzi — Dreaming of My Wife on the Twentieth Night of the First Month**

Ten years have passed; in life and death we drift apart, apart—
Yet though I do not dwell on it, I cannot forget.
A lonely grave a thousand miles away,
Where can I speak of my desolation?
Even if we met, you would not know me:
Dust upon my face, my temples white as frost.

Last night in a quiet dream I suddenly returned home—
By the small latticed window,
You were combing your hair, putting on your makeup.
We gazed at each other, unable to speak;
Only tears streamed, a thousand lines.
I know each year my heart will break
On nights of bright moonlight,
On the low pine-covered hill."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The great river rolls eastward; its waves have washed away
a thousand ages of gallant figures.
West of the old ramparts, men say,
lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, wild waves crash upon the shore,
churning up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and waters are like a painting—
how many heroes at one time!

I think far back to Gongjin in his day,
Xiao Qiao newly wed, his heroic bearing bright and bold.
Feather fan and silk cap,
with a laugh and a word, masts and hulls flew to ash and smoke.
In spirit I roam that ancient realm—
you should laugh at me for loving too deeply, my hair already graying early.
Life on earth is but a dream:
one cup I pour in libation to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "# Eternal Joy at Beigu Terrace, Jingkou, in Remembrance of the Past

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains stand—
No hero found where Sun Quan once held ground.
The singing terraces, the dancing stands,
Their elegance all swept off by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, on common ways,
They say the man called Jinu once lived here.
Think of those years of golden spears and iron steeds—
A tiger's maw that swallowed up the miles.

Yuanjia's campaign, rashly pressing to the peaks,
Sealed the Wolf Summit—yet it earned a panicked glance behind.
Forty-three years, still gazing I recall
The beacon fires that flared along Yangzhou's road.

How can one bear to look back and see?
Beneath the Foli Temple's shrine the crows croak loud,
With drums of the spring sacrifice rung through the trees—
Who asks: is old Lian Po still able to eat his fill?"}

The land and rivers are as a painting — how many heroes of that time!

I think far back to Gongjin in those years, when Xiao Qiao had just married him, his majestic bearing bright and vigorous.

With feather fan and silk cap, amid his easy talk and smiles, the enemy's masts and hulls vanished in smoke and ashes.

A thousand ages, this land and rivers,
No hero found—where was Sun Zhongmou?
Dance pavilions, song terraces,
Their elegance all swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In ordinary lanes and streets,
Men say Junu once dwelt here.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-hooved steeds,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia acted rashly,
To crown himself at Langjuxu,
Only to flee northward in panic.
Forty-three years have passed,
In my gaze I still remember—
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Fili,
Crows of omen circle, drums of festival sound.
Who will ask: "Is Lian Po grown old,
Can he still eat his fill?""}

{"source": {"title": "江城子·乙卯正月二十日夜记梦", "author": "苏轼", "text": "十年生死两茫茫，不思量，自难忘。
千里孤坟，无处话凄凉。
纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜。
夜来幽梦忽还乡，小轩窗，正梳妆。
相顾无言，惟有泪千行。
料得年年肠断处，明月夜，短松冈。"}, "translation": "Ten years apart, both in this world and beyond, in silence and mist,  
I do not ponder, yet I cannot forget.  
A thousand miles, your lonely grave—  
nowhere to speak of this desolate chill.  

Even if we met, you would not know me—  
dust on my face, temples frosted white.  

Last night, a hushed dream brought me home:  
by the small windowed chamber, you were combing your hair.  
We gazed, wordless,  
with only tears streaming down.  

I know each year the place where hearts break—  
under the bright moon, on the pine-covered hill."}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy: Reflections at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

An age of rivers and mountains—yet no hero left to find,
No place where Sun Zhongmou's spirit lingers in the mind.
The dancer's terrace, the singer's hall,
Their splendor swept away by wind and rain's relentless fall.

Beneath the slanting sun, the grass and trees,
Down ordinary lanes and streets,
They say the place where "Jinu" once lived at ease.
I see it now—those days of golden spears and iron steeds,
A tiger's breath that swallowed leagues with ease.

Yuanjia's campaign, so rash, so bold,
In vain they sought like Huo to raise a monument of old,
And fled in panic, glancing backward to the cold.

Forty-three years have passed—and still my gaze recalls
The beacon fires that blazed along Yangzhou's walls.
How can I bear to look again—
Beneath the shrine of Foli, crows of omen croak,
And drums of festival in pagan chorus strike the plain.

Who is there left to ask, "Has Lian Po grown too old?
Can he still eat his fill, his youthful valor yet untold?""}

By Xin Qiji  

Ancient mountains and rivers stand—  
No trace remains of heroes, nor Sun Zhongmou’s domain.  
Dance pavilions, singing terraces:  
All such elegance swept away by wind and rain.  

Beneath slanting sun, through grass and trees,  
In those ordinary lanes, they say, once lived Jiannu.  
Think of that year: golden spears, iron-hooved steeds—  
His spirit swallowing ten thousand *li* like a tiger.  

In Yuanjia’s haste, to seal Mount Langjun’s peak,  
He gained only a hurried glance back in flight.  
Forty-three years—still I recall the road  
To Yangzhou, where beacon fires burned in the night.  

How can I look back? At Foli’s shrine,  
Crows swarm the drums of tribal rites.  
Who will ask: “Is old Lian Po still able  
To eat, and wield his might?”

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**To the Tune of "Yong Yu Le": Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou**

A thousand autumns, these rivers and mountains;  
No place can one find the hero, Sun Zhongmou.  
The terraces of dance and song—  
All their elegance swept away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,  
In ordinary lanes and paths,  
They say the house of Jinu once stood.  
Think of those years: golden swords, iron-clad steeds,  
Breath that swallowed miles like a tiger.

Yuanjia's rash campaign—  
To seal the wolf at Mount Ju,  
Only won a panicked glance to the rear.  
Forty-three years have passed—  
In the distance I still remember,  
Beacon fires over Yangzhou's roads.  
How can one bear to look back?  
Beneath the Foli Shrine,  
A flock of temple crows and drums of sacrifice.

By whom shall I be asked—  
Is Lian Po old, indeed?  
Can he still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The great river flows eastward,
Its waves have washed away the romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old fort,
They say, is Red Cliff where Zhou Yu fought the Three Kingdoms.
Rugged rocks pierce the sky,
Fierce waves crash against the shore,
Rolling up piles of white snow.
The land and river are like a painting,
How many heroes there were in that time.

I think of Gongjin in those days,
When Xiao Qiao had just become his bride, his heroic bearing was bright and spirited.
With a feather fan and a silk cap,
In a moment of talk and laughter,
The enemy’s masts and oars were turned to ash and smoke.
Wandering in spirit to that ancient country,
It should be said I am too sentimental, for my hair has early turned grey.
Life in this world is like a dream,
Let me pour a cup of wine to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**Yong Yu Le · Reflections at Jinkou's Beigu Pavilion**

Through all the ages, rivers and mountains remain—
But where is the hero, Sun Zhongmou, to be found?
The terraces of dance, the stages of song,
Their elegance, swept away by wind and rain and storm.

Slanting sun, withered grass, a few straggling trees—
An ordinary lane, an ordinary town;
Men say the place where once Ji'nu lay down.
I think of years gone by: golden spears, iron-hooved steeds,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand miles—fierce as a tiger's rage.

Yuanjia's rash campaign, aiming to "seal Wolf Ridge with honors gained"—
And what was won? A frantic glance thrown backward in retreat.

Forty-three years gone by—still from this vantage-point
I recall the beacon-fires blazing along the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back?
Beneath the Foli Shrine,
Crows at their feasting, drums of village festivals rising.

And who is there to ask?
"I am old as Lian Po now—
Can I still eat my fill?""}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "# The Great River — Reflections at Red Cliff

The great river surges eastward,
Washing away with its waves the ages' gallant souls.
West of the ancient fortress — so the story goes —
Lies Zhou Yu's Red Cliff, where the Three Kingdoms rolled.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
Terrifying waves crash upon the shore,
Churning up a thousand heaps of snow-white foam.
The rivers and mountains are a painted scene —
What a host of heroes thrived in that age!

I dream of Gongjin in his years of might,
When Xiao Qiao was newly wed, his bearing proud and bright.
With feather fan and silken cap,
Amid his talk and easy laughter,
Enemy masts and hulls reduced to ash and smoke, destroyed.
My spirit wanders to that fallen realm —
The tender-hearted ones would laugh at me,
For white hair sprouts upon my head too soon.
Life in this world is but a dream;
I pour this cup to greet the river's moon."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "**Nian Nu Jiao — Reflections at Red Cliffs**

The river surges eastward without cease,
Its waves have washed away, through time's long sweep,
The ages' heroes of renown and grace.
West of the old ramparts, as men believe,
Stood Zhou Yu's Red Cliffs, where the Three Kingdoms weaved.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, the waves crash wild and high,
Churning up snow-white foam in heaps a thousand deep.
Such landscapes! Painted scenes — how many heroes then,
How many a valiant soul who lived and died as men!

I think of Gongjin in his youthful prime,
When he had wed Xiao Qiao, in all his martial glory,
With shining gait and martial pride sublime.
Feather fan, silken cap — he spoke and smiled,
And enemy ships to ash and smoke were wild,
Went drifting in the mist, swept up by history's tide.
In spirit roaming back to that ancient land,
How love should mock me now, for grey has come too soon upon my brow.
All life is but a dream — let me raise a cup to the river moon"}

The romantic heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the ancient ramparts, people say,
Lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms' rage.

Rocks pierce the sky, wild waves slap the shore,
Rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The land and rivers are like a painting — how many heroes were there
In that brief time, in glory's golden glow!

I think of Zhou Yu in his youth, when Xiao Qiao had just become his bride,
So valiant, so dashing and bright.
Fan in hand, silk cap on head, in ease he would confide —
And in his talk and smile, the enemy's masts and oars turned to ash and smoke in flight.

My soul wanders to that ancient land; forgive my sentiment, I laugh at myself,
For white hairs have come too soon.
All the world is but a dream — I pour this cup to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "**Yong Yu Le: Reflections at Beiguting Pavilion, Jingkou**

Ages of rivers and mountains—no hero can be found; where once stood Sun Zhongmu.
The dancing terraces and singing stages, all elegance swept away by wind and rain.
Under slanting sun, amidst grass and trees, in common lanes and alleys, people say the dwelling of Ji'nu once stood.
Thinking of those years: golden spears and iron horses, a breath that swallowed ten thousand *li* like a tiger.
Yuanjia's hasty campaign to seal wolves on Mount Ju only won a flight glancing north in panic.
Forty-three years: before my eyes I still remember the beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.
How can one bear to look back? Beneath the shrine of Foli, a cloud of temple crows and drums of sacrifice.
Who will ask, has old Lian Po grown so aged that he can still eat?"}

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "# Yong Yu Le: At Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou, Reflecting on the Past

The rivers and the mountains, through ten thousand years, endure,
But where the hero? Where can one discern
The might of Sun Quan? Nothing here's so sure
As that his greatness, like a flame, must burn

And flicker out. Those song-and-dance pavilions, halls
Where elegance once held its splendid sway,
All beauty — swept away before it falls
By wind and rain that strip the ages gray.

The slanting sun on grass along the common way,
Where ordinary lanes and alleys lay —
They say the man called "Jinu" once dwelt here.

Think of that age: gold spears in fierce display,
Iron-harnessed steeds, a tiger's breath that could
Swallow ten thousand li — a fury none could stay.

Yuanjia's campaign, launched so heedlessly, so rash,
A seal upon Mount Langjuxu to claim —
But won a panicked glance northward, through the ash
Of rout, not glory, when the battle came.

Forty-three years gone, and still the flame
Of beacon fires on Yangzhou's road I see
Burn bright — a memory time cannot put out or maim.

How can I bear to turn my eyes? Beneath me
Stands the northern conqueror's shrine, where sacred crows
Cry out and festival drums echo — and I cannot be
At peace. And who will ask me, as the winter snows
Of age descend: "Old Lian Po — with years that have made you old and gray —
Can you still eat your fill? Can you still make your stand?""}

{"source": {"title": "江城子·乙卯正月二十日夜记梦", "author": "苏轼", "text": "十年生死两茫茫，不思量，自难忘。
千里孤坟，无处话凄凉。
纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜。
夜来幽梦忽还乡，小轩窗，正梳妆。
相顾无言，惟有泪千行。
料得年年肠断处，明月夜，短松冈。"}, "translation": "Ten years apart, both vast and dim,  
though I do not dwell on you, yet I cannot forget.  
A thousand miles, your lonely grave—  
no place to speak of my desolation.  

Even if we met, you would not know me:  
my face dust-covered, my temples frosted white.  

Last night in a hushed dream you suddenly came home—  
by the small window, you were doing your hair.  
We gazed at each other, speechless,  
with only a thousand lines of tears.  

I know that year after year where my heart breaks:  
on moonlit nights,  
among the short pines on the hill."}

Through endless ages, these rivers and mountains remain,

A thousand ages of rivers and mountains—
no hero to be found where Sun Zhongmou dwelt.
The terraces of song and dance,
the elegant airs, all swept away
by wind and rain.

Slanting sun, grass and trees,
ordinary lanes and alleys—
people say Ji'nu once lived here.
Think of those years:
golden spears, iron-clad horses,

Yuanjia acted rashly,

Forty-three years—
gazing from afar, I still remember

Under the Feli Shrine,
a flock of crows and the drums of spring sacrifice.

By whom shall I be asked—
"Is old Lian Po still able to eat his fill?""}

A thousand miles, the lone grave—  
nowhere to speak my chill sorrow.  
Even if we met, you wouldn't recognize me:  
dust on my face, frost in my hair.  

Last night, a faint dream brought me home—  
by the small window, you were combing your hair.  
We looked at each other, wordless,  
only tears streaming, a thousand lines.  
I know, each year, where my heart breaks:  
moonlit night, the short-pine hill."}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。

人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows eastward, its waves washing away the heroic figures of a thousand ages.

West of the old fortresses, men say, lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu in the Three Kingdoms.

Rugged rocks pierce the sky, crashing waves slap the shore, rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.

The land is like a painting—how many heroes appeared in that single age.

I imagine the young Gongjin then, just married to Xiao Qiao, his heroic bearing bright and sharp.

With feather fan and silk cap, amidst his talk and laughter, the enemy masts and oars vanished into ashes and smoke.

My soul wanders to that ancient realm—if love of the past moves me, they'd laugh that my hair has already turned white.

Life is but a dream—let me pour a libation to the river and the moon."}

and gaze until spring sorrow rises darkly
from the edge of sky.
Grass colour and misty light in the fading glow—

I mean to put my wildness to use, seeking one drunkenness;
drinking wine, singing out—yet forced merriment still has no savor.
My belt grows looser and looser, yet at last I do not regret:
for her I will waste myself away, and count it worth the cost."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal Joy · Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou
— Xin Qiji

Through all time, this land of rivers and mountains,
Where heroes dwell, I seek in vain
The place of Sun Zhongmou.

Dancing terraces, singing stages,
All elegance and flair,
Washed away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In common streets and lanes,
Men say Ju Nu once lived.

I think of that year —
Golden spears, iron-clad steeds,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuan Jia, rash and hasty,
Hoped to seal the Wolf Mount,
But won only a panicked glance to the north.

Forty-three years have passed,
Gazing afar, I still remember
The beacon fires on the road to Yangzhou.

How can I bear to look back?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
Ravens croak and drums sound at the festival.

Who will ask —
Is Lian Po grown old?
Can he still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Yong Yu Le · Thinking of the Past at Beigu Pavilion in Jingkou

A thousand autumns over rivers and mountains,
No hero to be found — where is Sun Zhongmou?
Dance pavilions and singing terraces,
Their elegance all washed away by wind and rain.

Slanting sun, grass and trees, ordinary lanes —
People say Jienu once lived here.
Think of those years: golden spears, iron-clad horses,
A roar that could swallow ten thousand li like a tiger.

Yuanjia's hasty campaign, to seal off Wolf Ridge,
Only won a panicked glance back northward.
Forty-three years — in the distance I still remember,
The beacon fires along the Yangzhou roads.

How can I bear to look back? Beneath the Fuli Shrine,
A stretch of temple crows and festival drums.
To whom can I ask: is old Lian Po,
Still able to eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The Great River flows east, its waves washing away the great figures of a thousand ages.
West of the old ramparts, they say, lies the Red Cliff of Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, startled waves strike the shore, rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
The rivers and hills are like a painting — how many heroes were there at that time.

I think far back to Gongjin in those years, when Xiao Qiao had just married him, his heroic bearing bright and vigorous.
With a feather fan and silk headdress, amid easy talk and smiles, the enemy's masts and oars vanished in ash and smoke.
Wandering in imagination through that ancient land, if my too many feelings should make me laugh at myself — my hair has already turned white.
The human world is but a dream; I pour one cup of wine to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "The River and the mountains stand through the ages, yet no one finds
where once the hero Sun Zhongmou held his ground.
The terraces where dancers swayed, the stages where they sang —
all that grace has been beaten down by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass, and trees, an ordinary lane and path:
men say it was here that the slave boy once dwelt.
Think of those years — golden spears and iron-clad horses,
whose breath could swallow ten thousand li, fierce as tigers.
Yet the Yuanjia campaign was rashly launched;
though they meant to seal the wolf-crest of Mount Ju,
they won in the end only to flee northward, glancing back in panic.
Forty-three years: from this vantage I still remember
the beacon fires along the Yangzhou roads.
How can one bear to look again?
Beneath the shrine of Foli,
only crows of the temple and drums of the village sacrifice.
Who will ask — am I, like Lian Po, now too old,
and can I yet eat my fill of rice?"}

{"source": {"title": "念奴娇·赤壁怀古", "author": "苏轼", "text": "大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。"}, "translation": "The great river flows east, its waves having washed away
the heroes of a thousand years.
To the west of the old ramparts, they say,
was Zhou Yu's Red Cliffs of the Three Kingdoms.
Jagged rocks pierce the sky, fierce waves crash the shore,
rolling up thousands of piles of snow.
The land is like a painting—how many heroes were there in that time.

I think of Gongjin in his youth,
just married to Xiao Qiao, his noble presence bright and brave.
With a feather fan and silk cap, in a moment of talk and laughter,
the enemy's ships were turned to ash and smoke.
My spirit wanders to that ancient land; my heart must laugh at me,
for my temples have already turned gray.
The world is like a dream—I raise one cup to the river and the moon."}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "# Reflections on History at Beigu Pavilion, Jingkou

Through the ages these rivers and mountains remain,
But where is the hero—where is Sun Quan's domain?
Dance halls and singing terraces, all elegance gone,
Swept off by wind and rain, their glory carried on—
To nothing.

Slanting sunlight on grass and trees, in lanes and streets unknown,
People say the warlord Ji Nu once called this place his own.
Think of those fierce years, when golden spears and iron-clad steeds
Devoured ten thousand li of earth like tigers seizing deeds
Of empire.

Yuanjia's campaigns, launched rashly to seal the Wolf Mount's crest,
Only won a panicked glance cast northward in distress—
A rout.

Forty-three years, and from this height I still recall
The beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou through the fall.
How can one bear to look back? Below the Foli shrine's dark door,
Crows of the spirit feast, and drums of sacrifice once more
Ring hollow.

Who will ask this aging man, whose beard grows white as snow—
Can old Lian Po, though past his prime, still eat his fill and go
To war?"}

四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。

A thousand years of rivers and mountains, heroes no more—
where Sun Zhongmou stood.
Terraces of dance and song, their grace all swept away
by wind and rain.

Slanting sun on grass and trees, in ordinary lanes,
they say Junu once lived.
Think of that year: golden halberds, iron steeds,
a tiger's breath swallowing ten thousand li.

Yuanjia's hasty campaign, to seal wolves at Langjuxu,
won only panic, glancing back north.
Forty-three years, still I remember in my gaze—
the beacon fires along the Yangzhou road.

How can I bear to look back: beneath Fuli's shrine,
crows and ritual drums.
Who will ask: has Lian Po grown old,
can he still eat his fill?"}

{"source": {"title": "永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古", "author": "辛弃疾", "text": "千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？"}, "translation": "Eternal rivers and mountains—yet no hero to be found
Where once Sun Zhongmou held his ground.
Dancing terraces, singing halls, all grace
Swept off by rain and wind, lost without trace.
Slanting sun on grass and trees,
In common lanes and streets—
People say Jiwu once dwelt here, beneath these skies.
Think of those years gone by:
Golden spears, iron steeds, a tiger's roar,
A spirit swallowing ten thousand li and more.
Yuanjia's campaign was rash and vain,
Seeking to seal at Wolf Mountain's height—
Only a panicked glance back north remained.
Forty-three years have fled; still in my sight
Beacon fires along the road to Yangzhou burn.
How can I bear to turn
And look again—beneath the Foli shrine,
Crows caw and festival drums divine.
Who will ask me now, this aged one—
"Lian Po is old, can he still eat well?"
I am old—
Can I still fill my bowl?"}

{"source": {"title": "春望", "author": "杜甫", "text": "国破山河在，城春草木深。
感时花溅泪，恨别鸟惊心。
烽火连三月，家书抵万金。
白头搔更短，浑欲不胜簪。"}, "translation": "**Spring View**

The nation is broken; hills and rivers remain.
Spring in the city — grasses grow deep and rank.
Moved by the times, flowers draw my tears;
grieving at parting, birds startle my heart.
Beacon fires have burned three months unending —
a letter from home would be worth ten thousand gold.
I scratch my white hair, and it thins the more,
until soon it will scarcely hold a pin."}

感时花溅泪，恨别鸟惊心。

Spring fills the city — grass and trees run deep.
Moved by the times, flowers splash with tears;
Grieving at parting, birds startle the heart.

A letter from home would be worth ten thousand in gold.
I scratch my whitening hair — it thins the more I scratch,
Until a hairpin can scarcely hold it in place."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "**Climbing High** *— Du Fu*

The wind is keen, the sky is high — gibbons cry in woe,
The islet clear, the sand gleams white, birds wheel and go.

Boundless, the withered leaves come rustling down,
Endless, the Yangtze rolls in with a thunderous sound.

Ten thousand miles from home, forever grieving at autumn as a guest,
All my life, so often ill, I climb this terrace all alone.

Hardship and bitter hate have thickened my frost-white temples;
In my wretchedness, I've lately set aside my cup of turbid wine."}

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。
浔阳地僻无音乐，终岁不闻丝竹声。
住近湓江地低湿，黄芦苦竹绕宅生。
其间旦暮闻何物？杜鹃啼血猿哀鸣。
春江花朝秋月夜，往往取酒还独倾。
岂无山歌与村笛？呕哑嘲哳难为听。
今夜闻君琵琶语，如听仙乐耳暂明。
莫辞更坐弹一曲，为君翻作琵琶行。
感我此言良久立，却坐促弦弦转急。
凄凄不似向前声，满座重闻皆掩泣。
座中泣下谁最多？江州司马青衫湿。"}, "translation": "# Song of the Pipa

By the Xunyang River I bid farewell to my guest at night,
Maple leaves and reed flowers shiver in the autumn light.
My host dismounted, my guest aboard the boat;
We raised our cups to drink — but no strings, no song, no note.
Drunk, yet uncheerful, sorrowful we part;
When we parted, the river bore the moon, vast and apart.
Then came the sound of a pipa from the water's deep,
My host forgot to leave, my guest forbore to sleep.
We traced the sound, softly asked who played it so;
The playing ceased — she hesitated to speak or show.
We drew our boat beside hers, invited her to meet;
Added wine, relit the lamp, and set our feast.
After many calls she finally came out,
Still clutching her pipa, half-hiding her face in doubt.
She turned the pegs, plucked three or four tones — unformed,
Yet before any melody, emotion was born.
Each string repressed, each sound a sigh of yearning,
As if telling a life of endless unfulfilled burning.
Brows lowered, she strummed on carelessly, string after string,
Pouring out all the endless sorrows she carried within.
Light gathering, slow pinching, brushing, then flicking the strings,
First the *Rainbow Skirt*, then the *Six Yāo* — the music she brings.
The great strings thundered like sudden rain pouring,
The little strings murmured like whispers adoring.
Thunder and murmur, entwined in their play,
Like pearls great and small, falling on jade in decay.
Like orioles warbling beneath blossoms, a slippery sound,
Like a channeled spring choking under ice, barely a sound.
The ice-choked stream froze, the strings grew mute and cold,
Mute and cold, the sound broke — silence took hold.
Then a secret sorrow, a hidden resentment was born,
At that moment, silence was better than sound or horn.
Like a silver vase cracking, water gushing out,
Like iron cavalry charging, swords and spears in shout.
The tune concluded, a sweeping stroke across the strings —
Four strings all at once, like silk torn apart on wings.
East boats, west pleasure boats, all sat hushed and still,
Only the autumn moon in the river's heart shone white and chill.
Pondering, she tucked her pick between the strings;
She straightened her garments, composed her bearing as she sings.
She said she was a girl from the capital's bright land,
Her home was beneath the Hámálíng slopes, close at hand.
At thirteen she had mastered the pipa's art,
Her name ranked first in the Imperial Academy's part.
When a tune was done, even skilled musicians praised her skill,
When her beauty was done, even the autumn beauties felt ill.
Youthful lords of the Five Tombs competed with gifts of gold and silk,
One song earned her more crimson gauze than could be told.
Silver-tipped hairpins snapped as they beat time to her song,
Crimson silk skirts turned stained where wine had lain along.
Year after year of laughter and cheer,
The autumn moons and spring breezes passed without a care.
Then her brother went to war, her elder sister died,
Days turned to nights, and youth faded from her side.
No more carriages stopped at her door — sparse and bare,
She grew old and married a merchant, past her prime and fair.
The merchant prized his trade and lightly parted from her,
Last month he floated up to Fuliáng to buy his tea.
She guards alone an empty boat by the river's mouth,
The moon shines bright around the boat, the water cold as drouth.
Deep in the night she dreams of youth and its bright days,
Weeping in dreams, her rouge-stained tears streak across her face.

I had sighed already hearing her pipa play,
And hearing these words, I sighed again, twice today.
Both of us, cast far from our home, ruined and alone —
Why must we have met before, to be allowed to comfort one?
I left the imperial capital last year in disgrace,
Banished to live in Xunyang, sick and weak in this place.
Xunyang is remote, no music for my ears,
All year long I hear no lute, no bamboo flute — no cheers.
I dwell near Pén River, low and damp the ground,
Yellow reeds and bitter bamboo surround my hut all around.
What do I hear here morning, noon, and night?
Cuckoos crying blood, gibbons howling in the moonlight.
Spring river, blossom mornings, autumn moonlit nights,
Often I pour wine and drink alone — my plight.
Were there no mountain songs or village flutes to cheer?
They'd be only a nasal, grating noise, nothing to hear.
Tonight I hear your pipa's tale, so clear and bright —
Like hearing immortal music, my ears restored to light.
Do not refuse — sit down and play one more tune,

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。
浔阳地僻无音乐，终岁不闻丝竹声。
住近湓江地低湿，黄芦苦竹绕宅生。
其间旦暮闻何物？杜鹃啼血猿哀鸣。
春江花朝秋月夜，往往取酒还独倾。
岂无山歌与村笛？呕哑嘲哳难为听。
今夜闻君琵琶语，如听仙乐耳暂明。
莫辞更坐弹一曲，为君翻作琵琶行。
感我此言良久立，却坐促弦弦转急。
凄凄不似向前声，满座重闻皆掩泣。
座中泣下谁最多？江州司马青衫湿。"}, "translation": "**The Song of the Pipa**

At Xunyang River's head I saw my friend off that night,
Where maple leaves and reed flowers shivered in autumn's chill.
I dismounted at the tavern, he stepped aboard his boat;
We raised cups to drink, yet no music graced our toast.
We drank, but joy refused to come; a somber parting near,
As the river swallowed the moon in its vast, misty expanse.
Then—suddenly—from the water came the sound of a pipa's strings.
My host forgot to leave, my guest delayed his departure.
Following the sound, we asked softly who might play,
But the music stopped, as if reluctant to reply.
We moved our boat closer, invited the player to meet;
Added wine, relit the lanterns, and the feast began anew.
After a thousand calls she emerged, half-hiding behind her pipa,
Neck already turned, fingertips resting gently on the strings.
A few plucks, a few taps—before a tune was formed,
The heart already spoke in melody.
Each string sounded hushed, each note like a sigh,
As if telling of a life of unfulfilled desires.
With lowered brows, her fingers traced the strings with ease,
Speaking of countless things that filled her heart.
Lightly plucking, slowly twisting, she brushed and flicked the strings,
First playing "Rainbow Skirt," then "Six Small Themes."
The large strings roared like sudden rain,
The small strings whispered like secret talk.
Roar and whisper, tangled and clear, they danced together,
Like great and small pearls falling on a jade plate.
Like orioles singing smooth among the blossoms,
Like a spring gurgling, trapped beneath ice.
The icy spring froze, the strings congealed to silence,
As if choked, unable to flow—the music paused.
In that pause, a deeper sorrow, a hidden grievance rose,
Where no sound surpassed the power of silence.
Then—a silver flask shattered, water bursting forth,
Iron cavalry charging, blades and spears clashing loud.
The song ended, the拨 drew across, a final stroke,
Four strings snapped as one, like tearing silk.
Across boats on east and west, all sat in breathless awe,
Seeing only the white autumn moon on the river's heart.
She quietly replaced the拨 among the strings, straightened her clothes,
And rose with composure, face solemn.
She said, "I was once a woman of the capital,
My home was by the Toad's Hill.
At thirteen I mastered the pipa,
First among the ranks of the Teaching Hall.
My playing once awed the masters,
And my beauty made the willow maids jealous.
The young lords of Wuling competed for my favor,
One song earned me countless scarlet silks.
I beat time on my silver combs till they broke,
My blood-red skirts stained with spilled wine.
Year after year of laughter and mirth,
I wasted spring moons and autumn breezes without thought.
Then my younger brother left for war, my aunt passed away,
Days turned to nights, and my beauty faded.
Before my gate, the horses grew scarce,
Till I, grown old, became a merchant's wife.
But merchants prize profit over parting—
Last month he went to buy tea in Fuliang.
I wait alone at the river's mouth, my boat empty,
Circled by the cold moonlight and the water's chill.
Deep in the night, I dream of my youth,
And wake with tears, my makeup streaked with red."
I had sighed upon hearing her pipa,
Now her words made me sigh again.
"We are both wanderers at the world's end—
Why must we meet as strangers?"
I left the capital last year,
Exiled and ailing in Xunyang town.
Xunyang is remote, with no music to enjoy,
No sounds of strings or pipes through all the years.
I live near the Pen River, damp and low,
Surrounded by yellow reeds and bitter bamboo.
What do I hear from morning till night?
Doves crying blood, gibbons wailing sad.
On spring mornings with flowers, or autumn nights with moon,
I often take my wine and drink alone.
Are there no mountain songs or village flutes?
They clash and screech—they are too harsh to hear.
Tonight I hear your pipa's voice,
Like hearing immortal music that clears my ear.
Please do not refuse—sit and play one more song,
And I will compose a Song of the Pipa for you.
Moved by my words, she stood long in thought,
Then sat back, tightened her strings—the tempo grew urgent.
The sound was not like what we'd heard before,
All present wept as they listened once more.
Among us, whose tears fell the most?
The Jiangzhou Official's blue robe was soaked through."}

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。
浔阳地僻无音乐，终岁不闻丝竹声。
住近湓江地低湿，黄芦苦竹绕宅生。
其间旦暮闻何物？杜鹃啼血猿哀鸣。
春江花朝秋月夜，往往取酒还独倾。
岂无山歌与村笛？呕哑嘲哳难为听。
今夜闻君琵琶语，如听仙乐耳暂明。
莫辞更坐弹一曲，为君翻作琵琶行。
感我此言良久立，却坐促弦弦转急。
凄凄不似向前声，满座重闻皆掩泣。
座中泣下谁最多？江州司马青衫湿。"}, "translation": "# Song of the Pipa

At night on the Xunyang River I saw a guest off;
maple leaves and reed flowers rustled, autumn cold.
The host dismounted, the guest stood in the boat;
we raised our cups to drink, but no strings, no pipes.
Drunk, yet no joy made; the parting was bleak;
at parting, the wide river lay steeped in moon.
Suddenly we heard a pipa from the water—
the host forgot to go back, the guest did not leave.
Following the sound I asked in a whisper who played;
the pipa stopped, and she delayed her reply.
We moved our boat nearer and invited her out;
more wine poured, lamps relit, the feast begun again.
After a thousand calls she at last came out,
still cradling the pipa, half hiding her face.
Turning the pegs, plucking three or two strings—
before a tune was formed, the feeling came.
Each string pressed into sorrow, each note a thought,
as if telling of a lifetime of unfulfilled hopes.
Brow lowered, unhurried, she played on and on,
telling out the endless things within her heart.
Light pressing, slow kneading, sweeping and picking—
first *Rainbow Skirts*, and then *Six Yao*.
The thick strings clattered like a sudden rain;
the fine strings whispered like private talk.
Clatter and whisper, tangled and mixed—
great pearls and small pearls falling on a jade plate.
An oriole's speech glides smooth beneath the flowers;
a spring flows choked and hidden under ice.
The icy spring grows cold and thick, the strings congeal and snap;
congealed, blocked—sound for a while ceased.
A deeper sorrow, a secret resentment rose:
here silence was better than sound.
A silver vase suddenly burst, water gushing out;
iron cavalry charged out, blades and spears ringing.
At the song's end she swept the plectrum across the middle—
all four strings gave one cry, like tearing silk.
East boat, west scull, silent, no one spoke;
only the river's heart, the autumn moon, white.
Musing, she set the plectrum among the strings;
smoothed her robes, rose, and composed her face.
She said she had been a girl of the capital,
her home lying beneath Toad Hill.
At thirteen she had mastered the pipa,
her name first on the rolls of the Teaching Bureau.
When her song ended even skilled masters submitted;
her makeup done, she was ever envied by Qiuniang.
Young lords of the Five Tombs vied to send her gifts—
for one song, red silk past counting.
Jeweled silver combs beat time till they broke,
blood-red silk skirts turned wine-stained.
This year's laughter, then the next;
autumn moons and spring winds passed lightly by.
Her brother went off to war, her aunt died;
evenings went, mornings came, and her beauty faded.
Before her door the crowds thinned, saddles grew rare;
grown old, she married a merchant's wife.
The merchant prized profit and thought little of parting—
last month he went to Fuliang to buy tea.
Coming and going, she keeps watch by the river mouth beside an empty boat;
moon bright about the boat, the river water cold.
Deep in the night she suddenly dreamed of her youth;
she cried in the dream, tears of ruined makeup streaking red.
Hearing the pipa, I had already sighed;
hearing these words, I sighed again.
Both of us outcasts at the edge of the world—
meeting now, why must we have known each other before?
Since last year I left the imperial capital,
exiled and ailing in Xunyang town.
Xunyang is remote and has no music;
all year I hear no sound of strings or flutes.
I live near the Pen River, low and wet;
yellow reeds and bitter bamboo grow around my house.
What do I hear there, morning and evening?
The cuckoo crying blood, the gibbons mourning.
Spring river, flower mornings; autumn moon, clear nights—
often I take up wine and pour it, alone.
Are there not mountain songs and village pipes?
They clash and scrape, hard on the ear.
Tonight I hear your pipa's speech,
like hearing celestial music, my ears for a while made clear.
Do not refuse—sit and play one more song;
for you I set it down in this *Song of the Pipa*.
Moved by my words, she stood a long while;
then sat back, tightened the strings, and they grew faster.
Sorrowful, unlike the earlier sound—
all the company, hearing again, wept into their hands.
Who wept most among the guests?
The Sima of Jiangzhou, his blue gown soaked through."}

Maple leaves and reed flowers, autumn rustling.

Raised cups to drink, but no strings or tunes.

At parting, vast and boundless, the river bathed in moonlight.

Suddenly hearing pipa sound on the water,
The host forgot to return, the guest would not depart.
Following the sound, asking softly who was playing,
The pipa stopped, she hesitated to speak.
Moving the boat closer, inviting her to meet,
Adding wine, rekindling lamps, the feast began anew.

After a thousand calls and ten thousand entreaties, she finally emerged,
Still hugging her pipa, half-covering her face.
Turning the pegs, plucking the strings three or two sounds,
Before the melody formed, emotion already present.
Every string muffled, every sound thoughtful,
As if telling of lifelong unfulfilled aspirations.
Lowering her brows, playing carelessly and continuously,
Telling of all the endless matters in her heart.
Lightly gathering, slowly twining, stroking and picking,
First Rainbow Garment Dances then Six Minor Pieces.
The great strings clamorous like heavy rain,
The small strings whispering like private speech.
Clamorous and whispering, intermingled and played,
Like big pearls and small pearls falling on a jade plate.
Orioles' warbles beneath flowers, smooth and flowing,
Gurgling springs under ice, hard to pass.
Ice-cold springs, strings congealed and broken,
Broken and blocked, sound temporarily ceased.
A separate melancholy and hidden resentment arose,
At this moment, silence was better than sound.
The silver vase suddenly broke, water gushing forth,
Armored cavalry charging out, swords and spears clashing.
The tune ended, she swept the拨 across the center of strings,
Four strings at once, like tearing silk.
On all boats east and west, silent without a word,
Only seeing the autumn moon white in the river's center.

Tidied her garments, stood up, composed her expression.

Living under Xiha Maoling.
At thirteen she mastered the pipa,
Her name was listed first in the Music Academy.
After her performance, even experts would admire her,
When made up, she was always envied by Qiu Niang.
Five Tombs youths competed to give gifts,
For one song, countless bolts of red silk.
Silver hairpins beat time and broke,
Blood-red silk skirts stained with wine.
Year after year of joy and laughter,
Autumn moon and spring wind passed idly by.
Her brother went to the army, her aunt died,
Dawn to dusk, her beauty faded.

Growing old, she married a merchant.

Last month he went to Fuliang to buy tea.

Around the boat, bright moon, river water cold.

Dreaming and crying, makeup tears staining her face.

Exiled and ill in Xunyang city.

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。
浔阳地僻无音乐，终岁不闻丝竹声。

春江花朝秋月夜，往往取酒还独倾。

By Bai Juyi
Translated into English Verse

---
At Xunyang's riverbank I bid a friend good-bye,
The maple leaves and reed-blooms shiver in the autumn sky.
My guest dismounts; my friend embarks upon the boat—
We raise our cups to drink, but no pipa's note.
Too drunk for joy, we part in sorrow and in gloom,
The moonlight floods the river, shrouded, white as doom.
Suddenly from the water comes a pipa's plaintive sound—
My guest delays his setting-out; I halt upon the ground.

I follow where the music leads and softly call out, "Who?"
The pipa falls to silence—she dares not answer true.
We shift our boat to hers and ask her to appear;
The lamps are trimmed, the wine is poured; we seat ourselves near.
After countless calls entreated, slowly she comes out,
Embracing her pipa, half her face veiled round about.

She turns the pegs, plucks every string, two, three soft notes unfurl—
No tune is yet begun, but already feeling swirls.
Each string seems choked with longing, every note with sighing,
As though she poured her life's frustrations into crying.
Brow lowered, her fingers drift in effortless command,
Telling in music all the grief no tongue could stand.

She strokes and rolls and brushes, plucks and lets them ring,
First "Nei Chang," then "Liu Yao"—two melodies she'd bring.
The bass strings roar like sudden rain that pounds the earth,
The treble whispers soft as secrets given birth.
The roar and whisper tangle, interweave and dance,
Like pearls both great and small that fall and scatter, glance
To porcelain, striking, clinking, scattering bright—
Then trills like orioles that glide on wings of light
Among the flowers, then a murmur, slow and low,
Like springs beneath the ice that choke and will not flow.

The ice-bound current stiffens; strings go hard and dead;
All sound is frozen, choked—silence fills the thread.
And then from deeper sorrows, hidden grief takes birth—
That wordless pause speaks louder than all sound on earth.
Then sudden! Silver bottle bursts, water leaps free,
Like iron cavalry that charges, clashing sword and spear and sheath.
She swipes across the strings, a sweep to cut the air,
Four strings at once, a single crack, like splitting silk beyond repair.

On every boat around, all voices fade to none—
Only the autumn moon upon the river, white and done.
She tucks the pick in silence, straightens out her dress,
And rises, composure set upon her face's heaviness.

She speaks: "I am a woman from the capital's bright halls,
My home once stood beneath the slopes of Hama's walls.
At thirteen I'd mastered pipa's art, and claimed
A seat in Jiaofang's foremost troupe, my fame enflamed.
No singer could surpass me once my song was done;
When I put on my dress of beauty, Qiu Niang's envy spun.
The young lords of Wuling all bid up for my favor then—
For every song, red silks in countless heaps. But ah,
Those headlong years passed light and careless, fleeting, fast:
Silver and ornamental combs beat time until they'd cracked at last,
Blood-red silk skirts turned wine-stained, stained and torn and worn.
Year after year of laughter—then the autumn, then the dawn,
And then decline. My younger brother left for war, my elder sister dead,
And day by day my looks and fortunes dimmed with dread.
No riders at my gate, no carriages now wait—
I grew too old to sing, so married off, a merchant's wife. And yet
He cares for profit more than love, and always leaves again—
Last month he sailed to Fuliang's market, chasing tea's gain.
And so I wait beside the river, in this empty boat,
The moonlight cold around me, water cold to float.
Deep in the night I dreamed again of days gone by,
And woke to weep, my rouge-streaked tears staining my pillow dry."

I heard her pipa and already sighed in grief;
I heard her tale and felt my sorrow sharpen like a leaf.
We both are exiles, driven to the edge of sky—
Why must we first have known each other? Why?
Since last year, I've left the capital's bright towers,
Exiled, ill, confined to Xunyang's dark hours.
This place is far from court; there's not a single song—
All year I never hear a pipa, flute, or gong.
My house sits low and damp beside the marshland's spread,
Reeds and bitter bamboos thick around my bed.
What sounds do I hear morning, evening, night, and day?
The cuckoo crying blood; the gibbons' mournful bray.
On nights of spring-blossom moon and autumn's silver light,
I often pour my wine alone—no friend, no song in sight.
Of course there are hill songs and rustic village flutes—
But all that crude cacophony is worse than no repute.
Tonight, to hear your pipa is like hearing heaven's choir—
My ears, long closed, at last catch fire.
Do not refuse! Sit down again and play one more,
And I will turn your music into this, my Song of Pipa, I swear.

Moved by my words, she stood a long while in the hall,
Then sat and wound the strings to a new and faster call.
The music now, unlike before, more mournful, raw, and steep—
And every soul among us broke, and could not help but weep.
Among us all, who wept the most, whose tears fell deepest, wide?
The Marshal of Jiangzhou—his blue gown soaked, and dried,
And soaked again, his heart undone by all that sound and sight."}

无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。

The wind blows sharp, the sky hangs vast and high,
Gibbons cry out in anguish, wild and shrill;
The islet gleams, the sand shines white, birds wheel
And circle back. Endless the leaves that sigh
And rustle down; the mighty river, deep
And boundless, rolls its surging waters ever on.

Ten thousand miles, in autumn's grief, a guest
Forever wandering; a lifetime's woes
And aches—alone I climb this terrace. Troubles press,
Bitter regrets have thickened the frost at my temples. Sinking,
Spent and broken, I have but just now set
My cup of turbid wine aside, drinking no more."}

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。

On the Xunyang River bank, I bid a guest good-bye;
The maples and reeds shiver in the autumn night.
The host has dismounted, the guest is on his boat;
He lifts his cup to drink, but no pipa or lute notes.
Drunk without joy, we face a sad parting;
The river is vast, the moon is sinking in it.
Suddenly, from the water, a pipa’s sound is heard;
The host forgets to go home, the guest delays his departure.
Seeking the sound, I ask softly who is playing;
The pipa stops, and she hesitates to speak.
We move our boat nearer and invite her to come out;
We add wine, re-light the lamp, and begin the feast again.
After a thousand calls, she finally appears,
Holding her pipa, half hiding her face.
She tunes the strings, plucks them a few times;
Before a melody is formed, emotions arise.
Each string, each note is choked with sorrow;
As if telling a life of unfulfilled dreams.
With lowered eyes, she plays on, her fingers moving freely,
Telling all the endless tales in her heart.
She plucks, she rubs, she strums, she picks;
First the “Rainbow Skirt,” then the “Six One.”
The thick strings rumble like a sudden shower;
The thin strings whisper like a private talk.
The rumbling and whispering are intertwined;
Like pearls, big and small, falling on a jade plate.
Like an oriole’s song, smooth beneath the flowers;
Like a hidden stream, choked under the ice.
The ice-cold stream makes the strings stiff and mute;
The notes are blocked, and the music pauses for a while.
A hidden sorrow, a secret hate, now stirs;
In this moment, silence speaks louder than sound.
Suddenly, a silver bottle breaks, water gushes out;
Armored cavalry charges, swords and spears clash.
She ends the song by drawing her pick across the strings;
The four strings snap as one, like tearing silk.
In every boat around, a hushed silence falls;
Only the autumn moon, bright in the heart of the river.
She hesitates, puts her pick between the strings,
Straightens her clothes, rises, and composes her face.
She says she was once a girl of the capital,
Living below the Toad Hill.
At thirteen, she mastered the pipa’s art,
Ranked first in the Imperial Troupe.
When she finished a song, even masters were impressed;
When she dressed up, beauties were jealous of her.
Young lords from the Five Tombs competed to reward her;
For one song, she received countless silks of red.
She beat time with a silver comb until it broke;
Her blood-red silk skirt was stained with wine.
Year after year of laughter and joy;
The spring winds and autumn moons passed by without care.
My brother went to army, my aunt passed away;
Days went by, and her youth began to fade.
Fewer and fewer horses stopped at her door;
She grew old and married a merchant.
The merchant values profit over love; he is often away.
Last month he left for tea in Fuliang.
She waits alone in the empty boat by the river;
The moon is bright, the river water is cold.
In the deep night, she suddenly dreams of her youth;
In her dream, she weeps, her tear-stained makeup streaked red.
I had sighed when I heard her pipa;
Hearing her story, I sigh again.
We both are strangers, lost at the ends of the earth;
Why must we have known each other before?
Since last year, I left the capital,
Exiled and ill, I live in Xunyang.
This place is remote, with no music to hear;
All year long, I hear no strings or flutes.
I live near the low, damp Pen River;
Yellow reeds and bitter bamboo grow around my house.
What can I hear, from morning till night?
The cuckoo’s bloody cry, the gibbon’s mournful howl.
On flower-filled spring days, on moonlit autumn nights,
I often take my wine and drink alone.
Are there no mountain songs or village flutes?
Their crude, grating sounds are hard to bear.
Tonight, I hear your pipa’s words;
It’s like hearing immortal music, my ears are cleansed.
Do not refuse; stay and play one more song;
For you, I’ll turn this into a “Song of the Pipa.”
Touched by my words, she stands for a long time,
Then sits back, tunes her strings, and plays with haste.
The sorrowful notes are not like the ones before;
Hearing it again, everyone in the seats weeps.
Who in this room weeps the most?
The Prefect of Jiangzhou, with his blue robe wet with tears."}

Beneath the Xunyang River's edge at night, I see a guest away—
The maple leaves and reed-flowers shiver in autumn's dreary gray.
I dismount; my friend boards the boat; we raise our cups to drink,
But there's no lute or song to cheer us—only silence at the brink.



Drunk without gladness, we part with heavy hearts,
The vast river swallowing the moon's pale light.
Then, from the water, pipa notes arise—
The host forgets to leave, the guest delays his flight.



I follow the sound and softly ask who plays.
The music stops; she hesitates to speak.
I draw my boat near hers and ask her in.
More wine, relit lamps—the banquet renews its week.



After a thousand entreaties, out she comes,
Still holding the pipa, half-her face concealed.
She turns the pegs and plucks a note or two—
Before the tune begins, emotion is revealed.



Each string's low moan, each note a sigh so deep,
As if confessing all her unfulfilled life.
Brow low, fingers tracing line on endless line,
Pouring out countless sorrows, grief on grief.



Light strokes, slow pinches, flicks and sweeping grace—
First "Rainbow Skirt Dance," then "Little Willow" grace.
The low strings rumble like a sudden rain;
The high strings whisper like a secret's strain.



Rumbling and whispering, the notes entwine—
Like pearls, both large and small, on jade they fall and shine.
Then orioles warble smooth through blossoms overhead,
Then a choked spring seeps through ice, its murmurs barely fed.



The ice-cold spring congeals; the strings hold fast,
Frozen in silence—the notes cannot pass.
A deeper sorrow rises from the pause:
The silence speaks more than any sound could cause.



Like a silver vase struck open, water bursting free,
Or armored horsemen charging, swords and spears in fray—
She swipes the plectrum across the strings mid-heart,
All four strings crack as one, like silk torn away.



In every boat around, no one can speak—
Only the river's heart, where autumn's white moon gleams.
She tucks the pick between the strings and straightens up,
Smoothing her robes, composing her face's dream.

"Born in the capital, I am," she says,
"Housed at the foot of Haima Hill, my home.
At thirteen, I perfected on the pipa,
Placed first among the music school's famed dome.



When I finished a song, even masters praised;
When dressed for court, the finest beauties gazed
With envy. Young men from five noble towns
Fought to reward me; silks beyond counting round.



Jeweled pins and silver combs snapped keeping time,
My blood-red silk skirts stained with spilled wine.
Year after year with laughter and with play,
Through spring winds and autumn moons, I whiled the day.

But then my brother left for war and died;
My mentor fell; the years crept on in tide.
My beauty faded like a lamp run low,
Few carriages stopped at my door's long row.

At last, aging, I married a tea trader's wife,
And he—who values profit over life—
Goes to Fuliang to buy his leaves and leaves me here
To guard the empty boat all through the year.

The moonlight wraps the boat; the river's cold.
At depth of night I dream of what I've lost—
And wake to find my painted cheeks awash,
Tears streaming red down lashes in their cost."

I had sighed already at her music's art,
Now hearing all this story broke my heart.
Both of us wanderers, exiled and forlorn—
Why must we have met before to be reborn?

"Last year I bid farewell to the capital,
Banished and sick to Xunyang's distant wall.
This place is remote—no music graces the year;
No strings or flutes to comfort winter, spring, or clear.



I live near Pen River where the low ground stays damp,
Yellow reeds and bitter bamboo crowd my lamp.
What do I hear from morning until night?
The cuckoo's bleeding cry, the gibbons' mournful trill in flight.

On nights of spring-blossom moon or autumn's glow,
I often take my wine and drink alone below.
Are there no hill songs or village flutes around?
They only rasp and clang—a discordant sound.

Tonight, when I heard your pipa's song,
I felt as though immortal music made me young.
Please, sit a moment longer, play one more—
For you, I'll write this Song of Pipa ashore."

Moved by my words, she stands a long, long while,
Then sits and retunes—her fingers quick and wild.
The new strain, mournful, unlike the one before—
All present, hearing it, could not refrain from pouring tears.

Among us all, who wept the deepest, most?
The Jiangzhou Vice-Prefect—his blue robes stained and lost."}

{"source": {"title": "登高", "author": "杜甫", "text": "风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。"}, "translation": "**Climbing High**

The wind is sharp, the sky so high, the gibbons cry with woe,
The islets clear, the sands white, the birds wheel to and fro.

Boundless the falling leaves rustle down and down,
Endless the Yangtze rolls on, never to drown.

Ten thousand miles, a guest in autumn, I often roam;
A hundred years, with many ills, I climb this tower alone.

My toil and sorrow have thickened my frosty hair;
Down and out, I’ve lately stopped my cup of murky fare."}

{"source": {"title": "琵琶行", "author": "白居易", "text": "浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。
浔阳地僻无音乐，终岁不闻丝竹声。
住近湓江地低湿，黄芦苦竹绕宅生。
其间旦暮闻何物？杜鹃啼血猿哀鸣。
春江花朝秋月夜，往往取酒还独倾。
岂无山歌与村笛？呕哑嘲哳难为听。
今夜闻君琵琶语，如听仙乐耳暂明。
莫辞更坐弹一曲，为君翻作琵琶行。
感我此言良久立，却坐促弦弦转急。
凄凄不似向前声，满座重闻皆掩泣。
座中泣下谁最多？江州司马青衫湿。"}, "translation": "**The Pipa Ballad**

By the Xunyang River head at night I see a guest off,
Maple leaves and reed flowers, autumn rustles chill.
The host dismounts, the guest boards the boat;
He raises his cup to drink, but there's no string or pipe.
Drunk, yet no joy—soon parting, grim and bleak;
At parting, the vast river soaks the moon.
Suddenly from the water comes a pipa's song;
The host forgets to return, the guest won't set off.
Following the sound, I softly ask who plays;
The pipa stops, she hesitates to speak.
Moving the boat near, I invite her to meet;
More wine, relit lamps, the feast begins again.
After a thousand calls she finally appears,
Half hiding her face behind the pipa.
She turns the pegs, plucks three or two strings;
Before the tune takes shape, feeling is already there.
String after string, suppressed, each note a thought,
As if telling of a life of unfulfilled hopes.
Brow lowered, fingers plucking on at ease,
Telling all the countless things within her heart.
Light gathering, slow twisting, brushing, picking—
First the *Nishang*, then the *Liu Yao*.
Great strings rumble like driving rain,
Small strings murmur like whispered secrets.
Rumbling, murmuring, intertwined they sound—
Like great and small pearls falling on a jade plate.
Like orioles warbling smooth beneath the flowers,
Like blocked springs trickling under ice.
The icy spring chills, the strings congeal and stop;
Congealed, blocked—the sound pauses for a while.
A hidden sorrow, a secret resentment rises—
At this moment, silence is more than sound.
Then silver vases shatter, water bursts forth,
Armored riders charge, swords and spears clash.
The song ends, the拨 sweeps across the strings;
Four strings at once, like tearing silk.
Boats east and west, all silent, no one speaks;
Only the river's heart, the autumn moon, white.
Pondering, she tucks the拨 into the strings,
Straightens her garments, rises with composed bearing.
She speaks: "I was a girl of the capital,
My home was by Hama Ridge.
At thirteen I mastered the pipa,
My name was first in the Teaching Bureau's ranks.
My playing once made the masters bow,
My beauty each season made the courtesans envy.
The young nobles of Wuling competed to give gifts;
One song, and countless red silks were mine.
Jeweled combs struck time till they broke,
Crimson skirts were stained with spilled wine.
Year after year of laughter and song,
Autumn moons, spring breezes, all passed by.
My brother went to war, my aunt died;
Dusk to dawn, my youth and looks grew old.
Before my gate, carriages grew few and cold;
Grown old, I married a merchant as his wife.
The merchant values profit, not parting—
Last month he went to Fuliang to buy tea.
I wait alone at the river's mouth in this empty boat;
Around the boat, bright moon, river water cold.
In the deep night I suddenly dream of my youth;
In the dream I weep, my rouge-streaked tears fall in lines.
Hearing the pipa, I had already sighed;
Hearing these words, I sigh again and again.
Both of us, castaways at the edge of the world—
Why must we have met before to understand?
Since last year I left the imperial city,
A sick, banished man in Xunyang town.
Xunyang is remote, with no music;
All year I hear no string or flute.
My house near the river, low and damp,
Yellow reeds and bitter bamboo grow around my door.
What do I hear at dawn and dusk?
Cuckoos crying blood, gibbons mourning.
Spring river, flower mornings, autumn moonlit nights—
Often I take my wine and drink alone.
Are there no mountain songs or village flutes?
Their harsh, grating sound is hard to bear.
Tonight I hear your pipa's voice,
Like hearing immortal music, my ears briefly bright.
Do not refuse—sit and play once more;
For you, I'll compose this *Pipa Ballad*.
Moved by my words, she stands long in silence,
Then sits back, tightens the strings—they quicken.
Mournful, unlike the song before,
The whole assembly weeps, each wiping tears.
Who weeps the most among those present?
The Xunyang official—his blue gown is wet."}
